وَنَعوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شُرورِهمْ
items.en:
O Allah, we ask You to restrain them by their necks,
and we seek refuge in You from their evil.
items.tr:
Allāhumma innā naj`aluka fī nuḥūrihim 
wa na`ūdhu bika min shurūrihim.
items.ref: Abu Dawud 2/89, and Al-Hakim graded it authentic and Ath-Thahabi agreed 2/142.

بِكَ أَجولُ وَبِكَ أَصولُ وَبِكَ أُقاتِل
items.en:
O Allah, You are my strength and You are my support. 
For Your sake, I go forth and for Your sake, I advance and for Your sake, I fight.
items.tr:
Allāhumma anta `aḍudī, wa anta naṣīrī, 
bika ajūlu, wa bika aṣūlu, wa bika uqātil.
items.ref: Abu Dawud 3/42, At-Tirmidhi 5/572. See also Al-Albani, Sahih At-Tirmidhi 3/183.

cats.en: Invocations against the oppression of rulers

items.ar:
اللَّهُمَّ ربَّ السَّمَوَاتِ السَّبْعِ،
وَرَبَّ الْعَرْشِ الْعَظِيمِ،
 كُنْ لِي جَاراً مِنْ فُلاَنِ بْنِ فُلاَنٍ،
وَأَحْزَابِهِ مِنْ خَلاَئِقِكَ،
أَنْ يَفْرُطَ عَلَيَّ أَحَدٌ مِنْهُمْ أَوْ يَطْغَى،
عَزَّ جَارُكَ،
وَجَلَّ ثَنَاؤُكَ،
وَلاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ أَنْتَ
items.en:
O Allah, Lord of the seven heavens, 
Lord of the Magnificent Throne, 
be for me a support against [such and such a person] and his helpers from among your creatures, 
lest any of them abuse me or do me wrong.
Mighty is Your patronage,
and glorious are Your praises.
There is none worthy of worship but You.
items.tr:
Allāhumma Rabbas-samāwātis-sab`, 
wa Rabba ‘l-`Arshi ‘l-`Aẓīm, 
kun lī jāran min [here you mention the person's name], 
wa aḥzābihi min khalā'iqik, 
an yafruṭa `alayya aḥadun minhum aw yaṭghā, 
`azza jāruk, 
wa jalla thanā'uk, 
wa lā ilāha illā ant.
items.ref: Al-Bukhari, Al-'Adab Al-Mufrad (no. 707). Al-Albani graded it authentic in Sahih Al-'Adab Al-Mufrad (no. 545).
ti: O Allah, Lord of the seven heavens, …

items.ar:
الله أكبر،
الله أعز من خلقه جميعاً،
الله أعز مما أخاف وأحذر،
أعوذ بالله الذي لا إله إلا هو،
الممسك السموات السبع 
أن يقعن على الأرض إلا بإذنه،
من شر عبدك فلان،
وجنوده وأتباعه وأشياعه،
من الجن والأنس،
اللهم كن لي جاراً من شرهم،
جل ثناؤك وعز جارك، 
وتبارك اسمك، 
ولا إله غيرك
items.en:
Allah is the Most Great, 
Mightier than all His creation. 
He is Mightier than what I fear and dread. 
I seek refuge in Allah, Who there is none worthy of worship but Him. 
He is the One Who holds the seven heavens from falling upon the earth except by His command. 
[I seek refuge in You Allah] from the evil of Your slave [name of the person], 
and his helpers, his followers, and his supporters from among the jinn and mankind.
O Allah, be my support against their evil.
Glorious are Your praises
and mighty is Your patronage.
Blessed is Your Name,
there is no true God but You.
(Recite three times in Arabic.)
items.tr:
Allāhu Akbar, 
Allāhu a`azzu min khalqihi jamī`a, 
Allāhu a`azzu mimmā akhāfu wa aḥdhar, 
a`ūdhu billāhi ‘l-ladhī lā ilāha illā hū,
almumsikis-samāwātis-sab`i 
an yaqa`na `ala ‘l-arḍi illā bi idhnih,
min sharri `abdika [name of the person], 
wa junūdihi wa atbā`ihi wa ashyā`ih, 
mina ‘l-jinni wa ‘l-ins, 
Allāhumma kun lī jāran min sharrihim,
jalla thanā'uk,
wa `azza jāruk,
wa tabāraka-smuk, 
wa lā ilāha ghayruk.
items.ref: Al-Bukhari, 5/172.

سَرِيعَ الْحِسَاب
اهْزِم الأَحْزَاب
اللَّهُمَّ اهْزِمْهُمْ وَ زَلْزِلْهُم
items.en:
O Allah, Revealer of the Book, 
Swift to account, 
defeat the groups (of disbelievers). 
O Allah, defeat them and shake them.
items.tr:
Allāhumma munzila ‘l-kitāb, 
sarī`a ‘l-ḥisāb, 
ihzimi ‘l-aḥzāb, 
Allāhumma-hzimhum wa zalzilhum.
items.ref: Muslim 3/1362.

items.en: O Allah, suffice (i.e. protect) me against them however You wish.
items.tr: Allāhummak-finīhim bimā shi't.
items.ref: Muslim 4/2300.

cats.en: Invocations for if you are stricken by in your faith
cats.ar: دعاء من أصابه وسوسة في الإيمان

items.ar:
يَسْتَعِيذُ بِاللَّهِ.

يَنْتَهِي عَمَّا شك فِيهِ.
items.en:
(Say: ) I seek refuge in Allah. 
(Then you should desist from doing what you are in doubt about.)
items.tr: A`ūdhu billāh
items.ref: Al-Bukhari, cf. Al-Asqalani, Fathul-Bari 6/336, Muslim 1/120.

items.ar: يقول" آمنت بالله ورسله"
items.en: (Say: ) I believe in Allah and His Messengers.
items.tr: Āmantu billāhi wa Rusulih.

items.ar:
يقرأ قوله تعالى ((هُوَ الأوَّلُ، وَالآخِرُ،
وَالظّاهِرُ، وَالْباطِنُ،
 وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَيءٍ عَليم))
items.en:
(Recite the Ayat) He is the First and the Last, 
the Most High and the Most Near. 
And He is the Knower of all things (in Arabic).
items.tr:
Huwa ‘l-Awwalu wa ‘l-Ākhir,
waẓ-Ẓāhiru wal-Bāṭin, 
wa huwa bikulli shay'in `Alīm.
items.ref: Al-Hadid 57:3, Abu Dawud 4/329. Al-Albani graded it good in SahihAbu Dawud, 3/962.

cats.en: Invocations for the setting of a debt

items.ar:
اللّهُمَّ اكْفِني بِحَلالِكَ عَنْ حَرامِك،
وَأَغْنِني بِفَضْلِكَ عَمَّنْ سِواك
items.en:
O Allah, suffice me with what You have allowed instead of what You have forbidden, 
and make me independent of all others besides You.
items.tr:
Allāhummak-finī biḥalālika `an ḥarāmik, 
wa 'aghninī bi faḍlika `amman siwāk.
items.ref: At-Tirmidhi 5/560. See also Al-Albani, Sahih At-Tirmidhi 3/180.

وَالْعَجْزِ وَالْكَسَلِ،
وَالْبُخْلِ وَالْجُبْنِ،
وَضَلَعِ الدَّيْنِ وَغَلَبَةِ الرِّجَالِ
items.tr:
Allāhumma innī a`ūdhu bika mina ‘l-ḥammi wa ‘l-ḥazan, 
wa ‘l-`ajzi wa ‘l-kasal,
wa ‘l-bukhli wa ‘l-jubn, 
wa ḍala`id-dayni wa ghalabatir-rijāl.
items.ref: Al-Bukhari 7/158.

cats.en: Invocation against the distractions of Satan during the prayer and recitation of the Quran
cats.ar: دعاء الوسوسة في الصلاة و القراءة

items.ar:
أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ الشَّيطَانِ الرَّجِيمِ، 
وَاتْفُلْ عَلَى يَسَارِكَ
items.en:
(Say: ) I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the outcast 
(then blow with a little spittle to your left). 
(Do this three times reciting in Arabic.)
items.tr: A`ūdhu billāhi minash-shayṭānir-rajīm.
items.ref: Muslim 4/1729.

cats.en: Invocation for when you find something becoming difficult for you

items.ar:
اللَّهُمَّ لاَ سَهْلَ إِلاَّ مَا جَعَلْتَهُ سَهْلاً،
وَأَنْتَ تَجْعَلُ الْحَزْنَ إِذَا شِئْتَ سَهْلاً
items.en:
O Allah, there is no ease other than what You make easy. 
If You please You ease sorrow.
items.tr:
Allāhumma lā saḥla illā ma ja`altahu saḥla 
wa anta taj`alu ‘l-ḥazna idhā shi'ta saḥla.
items.ref: Ibn Hibban in his Sahih (no. 2427), and Ibn As- Sunni (no. 351). Al-Hafidh (Ibn Hajar) said that this Hadith is authentic. It was also declared authentic by 'Abdul-Qadir Al-Arna'ut in his checking of An-Nawawi's Kitabul-Athkarp. 106.

items.ar: مَا مِنْ عَبْدٍ يُذنِبُ ذَنْباً فَيُحْسِنُ الطُّهُورَ، ثُمَّ يَقُومُ فَيُصَلِّي رَكْعَتَيْنِ، ثُمَّ يَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ إِلاَّ غَفَرَ اللَّهُ لَهُ
items.en: There is not any slave of Allah who commits a sin, then he perfects his purification and stands to pray two Rak'ahs of prayer, then seeks Allah's forgiveness, except that Allah will forgive him.

cats.en: Congratulations for new parents and how they should respond

items.ar:
(بَارَكَ اللَّهُ لَكَ فِي الْمَوْهُوبِ لَكَ، 
وَشَكَرْتَ الْوَاهِبَ، 
وَبَلَغَ أَشُدَّهُ، 
وَرُزِقْتَ بِرَّهُ).
 

 وَيَرُدُّ عَلَيْهِ الْمُهَنَّأُ فَيَقُولُ:
(بَارَكَ اللَّهُ لَكَ وَبَارَكَ عَلَيْكَ، 
وَجَزَاكَ اللَّهُ خَيْراً، 
وَرَزَقَكَ اللَّهُ مِثْلَهُ، 
وَأَجْزَلَ ثَوَابَكَ).
items.en:
May Allah bless you with His gift to you, 
and may you (the new parent) give thanks,
may the child reach the maturity of years,
and may you be granted its righteousness. 

The reply of the person being congratulated is to say:

May Allah bless you, and shower His blessings upon you, 
and may Allah reward you well
and bestow upon you its like 
and reward you abundantly
items.tr:
Bārakallāhu laka fi ‘l-mawhūbi lak, 
wa shakarta ‘l-wāhib, 
wa balagha ashuddah, 
wa ruziqta birrah.

The reply of the person being congratulated is to say: Bārakallahu laka wa bāraka `alayk, 
wa jazākallāhu khayra, 
wa razaqakallāhu mithlah, 
wa ajzala thawābak.
items.ref: An-Nawawi, Kitdbul-'Athkarp. 349, and Sahihul-'Athkar2/7l3 by Saleem Al-Hilali.

items.ar:
كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يعوذ الحسن والحسين
" أعيذكما بكلمات الله التامة،
من كل شيطان وهامة، 
ومن كل عينِ لامة "
items.tr:
The Prophet (ﷺ) used to seek Allah's protection for Al-Hasan and Al-Husain by saying: U`īthukumā bikalimāti ‘llāhit-tāmmati 
min kulli shayṭānin wa hāmmah, 
wa min kulli `aynin lāmmah

items.en: Do not worry, it will be a purification (for you), Allah willing.
items.tr: Lā ba'sa ṭahūrun in shā Allāh.

I ask Almighty Allah, Lord of the Magnificent Throne, to make you well. 
(Recite seven times in Arabic .)

items.ref: At-Tirmidhi, Abu Dawud. See also Al-Albani, Sahih At-Tirmidhi 2/210 and Sahihul-Jami' As-Saghir 5/180.

أللّهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لي وَارْحَمْني 
وَأَلْحِقْني بِالرَّفيقِ الأّعْلى
items.en:
O Allah, forgive me and have mercy upon me, 
and join me with the highest companions (in Paradise).
items.tr:
Allāhumma’ghfir lī warḥamnī 
wa alḥiqnī bir-rafīqi ‘l-'A`alā.
items.ref: Al-Bukhari7/10, Muslim 4/1893.
ti: O Allah, forgive me and have mercy …

items.ar:
جعل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عند موته يدخل يديه في الماء فيمسح بهما وجههُ ويقول:
لا إله إلا الله إن للموت لسكرات
items.en:
There is none worthy of worship but Allah, 
surely death has agonies.
items.tr:
As he was dying, the Prophet (ﷺ) dipped his hands in water and wiped his face saying: Lā ilāha illallāh
inna li ‘lmawti la’sakarāt.
items.ref: Al-Bukhari, cf. Al-Asqalani, Fathul-Bari 8/144. The Hadith also mention him using the Siivak (tooth stick).

وَاللّهُ أَكْبَر،
لا إلهَ إلاّ اللّهُ وحْدَهُ،
لا إلهَ إلاّ اللّهُ

لا إلهَ إلاّ اللّهُ

items.en:
There is none worthy of worship but Allah, 
Allah is the Most Great. 
None has the right to be worshipped but Allah alone. 
None has the right to be worshipped but Allah alone, 
Who has no partner. 
There is none worthy of worship but Allah,
His is the dominion and His is the praise.
There is none worthy of worship but Allah,
there is no power and no might but by Allah.
items.tr:
Lā ilāha illallāh
wallāhu Akbar, 
lā ilāha illallāhu waḥdah,
lā ilāha illallāh
waḥdahu lā sharīka lah, 
lā ilāha illallāh
lahu ‘l-mulku wa lahu ‘l-ḥamd, 
lā ilāha illallāh
wa lā ḥawla wa lā quwwata illā billāh.
items.ref: At-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah. See also Al-Albani, Sahih At-Tirmidhi 3/152 and Sahih Ibn Majah 2/317.

cats.en: Invocation for when tragedy strikes

items.ar:
إِنّا للهِ وَإِنَا إِلَيْهِ راجِعون،
اللهُمِّ اْجُرْني في مُصيبَتي، 
وَاخْلُفْ لي خَيْراً مِنْها
items.en:
We are from Allah and unto Him we return. 
O Allah take me out of my plight 
and bring to me after it something better.
items.tr:
Innā lillāhi wa innā ilayhi rāji`ūn, 
Allāhumma-jurni fī muṣībatī 
wa 'khluf lī khayran minhā.
items.ref: Muslim 2/632.

cats.en: Invocation for closing the eyes of the dead

items.ar:
اللهُمِّ اغْفِرْ لِفلان (باسمه)
وَارْفَعْ دَرَجَتَهُ في المَهْدِيين، 
وَاخْلُفْهُ في عَقِبِهِ في الغابِرين، 
وَاغْفِرْ لَنا وَلَهُ يا رَبَّ العالَمين،
وَافْسَحْ لَهُ في قَبْرِهِ وَنَوِّرْ لَهُ فيه
items.en:
O Allah, forgive [name of the person]
and elevate his station among those who are guided. 
Send him along the path of those who came before, 
and forgive us and him, O Lord of the worlds.
Enlarge for him his grave, and shed light upon him in it.
items.tr:
Allāhumma’ghfir li (name of the person) 
warfa` darajatahu fi ‘l-mahdiyyīn,
wakhlufhu fī `aqibihi fi ‘l-ghābirīn, 
wagh’fir-lanā wa lahu yā Rabba ‘l-`ālamīn, 
wafsaḥ lahu fī qabrihi wa nawwir lahu fīh.
items.ref: Muslim 2/634.

cats.en: Invocations for the dead in the Funeral prayer

items.ar: ((اللَّهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لَهُ وَارْحَمْهُ، وَعَافِهِ، وَاعْفُ عَنْهُ، وَأَكْرِمْ نُزُلَهُ، وَوَسِّعْ مُدْخَلَهُ، وَاغْسِلْهُ بِالْمَاءِ وَالثَّلْجِ وَالْبَرَدِ، وَنَقِّهِ مِنَ الْخَطَايَا كَمَا نَقَّيْتَ الثَّوْبَ الأَبْيَضَ مِنَ الدَّنَسِ، وَأَبْدِلْهُ دَاراً خَيْراً مِنْ دَارِهِ، وَأَهْلاً خَيْراً مِنْ أَهْلِهِ، وَزَوْجَاً خَيْراً مِنْ زَوْجِهِ، وَأَدْخِلْهُ الْجَنَّةَ، وَأَعِذْهُ مِنْ عَذَابِ القَبْرِ [وَعَذَابِ النَّارِ])).
items.en:
O Allah, forgive him and have mercy on him, 
and give him strength and pardon him. 
Be generous to him, 
and cause his entrance to be wide, 
and wash him with water and snow and hail. 
Cleanse him of his transgressions 
as white cloth is cleansed of stains. 
Give him an abode better than his home, 
and a family better than his family, 
and a wife better than his wife. 
Take him into Paradise, 
and protect him from the punishment of the grave [and from the punishment of Hell-fire].
items.tr:
Allāhumma’ghfir lahu warḥamh, 
wa `āfihi, wa`fu `anh, 
wa akrim nuzulah, 
wa wassi` mudkhalah, 
wagh’silhu bi ‘lmā'i wath-thalji walbarad, 
wa naqqihi mina ‘l-khaṭāyā
kamā naqqaytath-thawba ‘l-abyaḍa minad-danas, 
wa abdilhu dāran khayran min dārih, 
wa ahlan khayran min ahlih, 
wa zawjan khayran min zawjih, 
wa adkhilhu ‘l-jannah, 
wa a`idhhu min `adhābi ‘l-qabri [wa `adhābin-nār].
items.ref: Muslim 2/663.
ti: O Allah, forgive him and have mercy …

items.ar:
اللهُمِّ اغْفِرْ لِحَيِّنا وَمَيِّتِنا، 
وَشاهِدِنا وَغائِبِنا، 
وَصَغيرِنا وَكَبيرِنا،
وَذَكَرِنا وَأُنْثانا.
اللهُمِّ مَنْ أَحْيَيْتَهُ مِنّا
فَأَحْيِهِ عَلى الإِسْلام،
وَمَنْ تَوَفَّيْتَهُ مِنّا فَتَوَفَّهُ عَلى الإِيمان،
اللهُمِّ لا تَحْرِمْنا أَجْرَه،
وَلا تُضِلَّنا بَعْدَه
items.en:
O Allah forgive our living and our dead, 
those who are with us and those who are absent, 
our young and our old, 
our menfolk and our womenfolk. 
O Allah, whomever you give life from among us 
give him life in Islam, 
and whomever you take away from us 
take him away in Faith. 
O Allah, do not forbid us their reward 
and do not send us astray after them.
items.tr:
Allāhumma’ghfir liḥayyinā, wa mayyitinā, 
wa shāhidinā, wa ghā'ibinā,
wa ṣaghīrinā wa kabīrinā, 
wa dhakarinā wa unthānā. 
Allāhumma man aḥyaytahu minnā 
fa aḥyihi `ala ‘l-Islām, 
wa man tawaffaytahu minnā
fatawaffahu `alal-īmān, 
Allāhumma lā taḥrimnā ajrah
wa lā tuḍillanā ba`dah.
items.ref: Ibn Majah 1/480, Ahmad 2/368. See also Al-Albani, Sahih Ibn Majah 1/251.
ti: O Allah forgive our living and our …

items.ar:
اللهُمِّ إِنَّ فُلانَ بْنَ فُلانٍ في ذِمَّتِك، 
وَحَبْلِ جِوارِك، 
فَقِهِ مِنْ فِتْنَةِ الْقَبْرِ وَعَذابِ النّار، 
وَأَنْتَ أَهْلُ الْوَفاءِ وَالْحَقِّ، 
فَاغْفِرْ لَهُ وَارْحَمْهُ، 
إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الغَفورُ الرَّحيم
items.en:
O Allah, surely [name the person] is under Your protection,
and in the rope of Your security,
so save him from the trial of the grave and from the punishment of the Fire.
You fulfill promises and grant rights,
so forgive him and have mercy on him.
Surely You are Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.
items.tr:
Allāhumma inna [name the person] fī dhimmatik, 
wa ḥabli jiwārik, 
faqihi min fitnati ‘l-qabri wa `adhābin-nār, 
wa anta ahlu ‘l-wafā'i wa ‘l-ḥaqq. 
Faghfir lahu warḥamh
innaka anta ‘l-Ghafūrur-Raḥīm.
items.ref: Ibn Majah, Abu Dawud 3/211. See also Al Albani, Sahih Ibn Majah 1/251.
ti: O Allah, surely [name the person] is …

items.ar:
اللهُمِّ عَبْدُكَ وَابْنُ أَمَتِك،
احْتاجَ إِلى رَحْمَتِك،
وَأَنْتَ غَنِيٌّ عَنْ عَذابِه،
إِنْ كانَ مُحْسِناً فَزِدْ في حَسَناتِه،
وَإِنْ كانَ مُسيئاً فَتَجاوَزْ عَنْه
items.en:
O Allah, Your male slave and the child of Your female slave is in need of Your mercy, 
and You are not in need of his torment. 
If he was pious then increase his rewards
and if he was a transgressor then pardon him.
items.tr:
Allāhumma `abduka wabnu 'amatik 
iḥtāja ilā raḥmatik, 
wa anta ghaniyyun `an `adhābih, 
in kāna muḥsinan fazid fī ḥasanātih, 
wa in kāna musī'an fatajāwaz `anh.
items.ref: Al-Hakim 1/359 who graded it authentic and Ath-Thahabi agreed with him. See also Al-Albani, Ahkamul-Jana'iz, p. 125.

cats.en: Invocations for a child in the Funeral prayer

items.ar: اللهُمِّ اجْعَلْهُ لَنا فَرَطاً، وَسَلَفاً وَأَجْراً
items.en: O Allah, make him for us a precursor, a forerunner and a cause of reward.
items.tr: Allāhumma’j`alhu lanā faraṭan, wa salafan, wa ajra.
items.ref: Al-Hasan (Al-Basri) used to recite Surat Al-Fatihah for a child's funeral and then say this. Al-Bukhari, Kitabul-Jana'iz, p. 65.
ti: O Allah, make him for us a …

cats.en: Invocation for the bereaved

items.ar:
"إن لله ما أخذ
وله ما أعطى.
وكل شيء عنده بأجل مُسمى...
فلتصبر ولتحتسب "



وإن قال:
"أعظم الله أجرك،
وأحسن عزاءك 
وغفر لميتك" 
فحسن
items.en:
Surely, Allah takes what is His, 
and what He gives is His, 
and to all things He has appointed a time... 
so have patience and be rewarded.

May Allah magnify your reward, 
and make perfect your bereavement, 
and forgive your departed.
items.tr:
Inna lillāhi mā akhadh, 
wa lahu mā a`tā, 
wa kullu shay'in `indahu bi ajalin musammā . . . 
faltaṣbir wa ‘l-taḥtasib .

[Also good to say: ] 
A`ẓamallāhu ajrak, 
wa 'aḥsana `azā'ak,
wa ghafara limayyitik.
items.ref: 1 Al-Bukhari 2/80, Muslim 2/636. 2An-Nawawi, Kitabul-'Athkar, p. 126.

cats.en: Invocation to be recited when placing the dead in his grave

items.ar:
بِسْمِ اللهِ 
وَعَلى سُنَّةِ رَسولِ الله
items.en:
With the Name of Allah, 
and according to the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah.
items.tr:
Bismillāh
wa `alā sunnati Rasūlillāh.
items.ref: Abu Dawud 3/314 with an authentic chain. Ahmad also recorded it with the wording: With the Name of Allah, and according to the religion of the Messenger of Allah. Its chain is also authentic.
ti: With the Name of Allah, and according …

cats.en: Invocation to be recited after burying the dead

items.ar:
اللَّهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لَهُ
اللَّهُمَّ ثَبِّتْهُ
items.en:
O Allah, forgive him. 
O Allah, strengthen him.
items.tr:
Allāhumma’ghfir lah
Allāhumma thabbit’h.
items.ref: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to stop after burying the dead and say to the people: "Ask Allah to forgive your brother and pray for him to be strengthened, for indeed he is now being questioned." Abu Dawud 3/315, and Al-Hakim 1/370 who graded it authentic and Ath-Thahabi agreed.
ti: O Allah, forgive him. O Allah, strengthen …

cats.en: Invocation for visiting the graves

items.ar:
السَّلامُ عَلَيْكُمْ أَهْلَ الدِّيارِ مِنَ المؤْمِنينَ وَالْمُسْلِمين، 
وَإِنّا إِنْ شاءَ اللهُ بِكُمْ لاحِقون، 
نَسْاَلُ اللهَ لنا وَلَكُمْ العافِيَة
items.en:
Peace be upon you, people of this abode, from among the believers and those who are Muslims, 
and we, by the Will of Allah, shall be joining you. 
[May Allah have mercy on the first of us and the last of us] 
I ask Allah to grant us and you well-being.
items.tr:
Assalāmu `alaykum ahlad-diyāri minal-mu'minīna wa ‘l-muslimīn, 
wa innā in shā' Allāhu bikum lāḥiqūn 
nas'alullāha lanā wa lakumul-`āfiyah.
items.ref: Muslim 2/671, Ibn Majah 1/494, the portion brackets is from Muslim 2/671.
ti: Peace be upon you, people of this …

cats.en: Invocations for when the wind blows

items.ar:
اللّهُمَّ إِنَّي أَسْأَلُكَ خَيْرَها، 
وَأَعوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّها
items.en:
O Allah, I ask You for the good of it, 
and seek refuge in You against its evil.
items.tr:
Allāhumma innī as'aluka khayrahā, 
wa a`ūdhu bika min sharrihā.
items.ref: Abu Dawud 4/326, Ibn Majah 2/1228. See also Al-Albani, Sahih Ibn Majah 2/305.
ti: O Allah, I ask You for the …

items.ar:
اللّهُمَّ إِنَّي أَسْأَلُكَ خَيْرَها،
وَخَيْرَ ما فيها،
وَخَيْرَ ما اُرْسِلَتْ بِه،
وَأَعوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّها،
وَشَرِّ ما فيها،
وَشَرِّ ما اُرْسِلَتْ بِه
items.tr:
Allāhumma innī as'aluka khayrahā, 
wa khayra mā fīhā, 
wa khayra mā ursilat bih, 
wa a`ūdhu bika min sharrihā, 
wa sharri mā fīhā, 
wa sharri mā ursilat bih.
items.ref: Muslim 2/616, Al-Bukhari 4/76.
ti: O Allah, I ask You for the …

cats.en: Invocation for when it thunder

items.ar:
سُبْحانَ الّذي يُسَبِّحُ الرَّعْدُ بِحَمْدِهِ،
وَالملائِكةُ مِنْ خيفَته
items.en: Glory is to Him Whom thunder and angels glorify due to fear of Him.
items.tr:
Subḥāna ‘l-ladhī yusabbiḥur-ra`du bi ḥamdihi 
wa ‘l-malā'ikatu min khīfatih.
items.ref: Whenever Abdullah bin Zubair (RA) would hear thunder, he would abandon all conversation and say this supplication. See Al-Muwatta' 2/992. It was graded authentic by Al-Albani as a statement of Abdullah bin Zubayr only.

cats.en: Some invocations for rain

items.ar:
اللّهُمَّ اسْقِنا غَيْثاً مُغيثاً مَريئاً مُريعاً،
نافِعاً غَيْرَ ضار،
عاجِلاً غَيْرَ آجِل
items.en: O Allah, shower upon us abundant rain, beneficial not harmful, swiftly and not delayed.
items.tr:
Allāhumma ‘asqinā ghaythan mughīthan marī'an murī`a, 
nāfi`an ghayra ḍārr, 
`ājilan ghayra ājil.
items.ref: Abu Dawud 1/303. See also Al-Albani SahihAbu Dawud 1/216.
ti: O Allah, shower upon us abundant rain, …

items.ar:
اللّهُمَّ أغِثْنا، 
اللّهُمَّ أغِثْنا، 
اللّهُمَّ أغِثْنا
items.en:
O Allah, send us rain. 
O Allah, send us rain. 
O Allah, send us rain.
items.tr:
Allāhumma aghithnā, 
Allāhumma aghithnā, 
Allāhumma aghithnā.
items.ref: Al-Bukhari 1/224, Muslim 2/613.
ti: O Allah, send us rain. O Allah, …

items.ar:
اللّهُمَّ اسْقِ عِبادَكَ وَبَهائِمَك، 
وَانْشُرْ رَحْمَتَكَ 
وَأَحْيِي بَلَدَكَ المَيِّت
items.en:
O Allah, give water to Your slaves, and Your livestock, 
and spread Your mercy, 
and revive Your dead land.
items.tr:
Allāhumma’sqi `ibādaka wa bahā'imak, 
wanshur raḥmatak, 
wa aḥyi baladaka ‘l-mayyit
items.ref: Abu Dawud 1/305. Al-Albani graded it good in Sahih Abu Dawud 1/218.
ti: O Allah, give water to Your slaves, …

cats.en: Invocation for when it rains

items.ar: اللّهُمَّ صَيِّباً نافِعاً
items.en: O Allah, (bring) beneficial rain clouds.
items.tr: Allāhumma ṣayyiban nāfi`a.
items.ref: Al-Bukhari, cf. Al-Asqalani, Fathul-Bari 2/518.

cats.en: Supplication after it rains

items.ar: مُطِرْنا بِفَضْلِ اللهِ وَرَحْمَتِه
items.en: We have been given rain by the grace and mercy of Allah.
items.tr: Muṭirnā bifaḍlillāhi wa raḥmatih.
items.ref: Al-Bukhari 1/205, Muslim 1/83.
ti: We have been given rain by the …

cats.en: Invocation for the withholding of the rain

items.ar:
اللّهُمَّ حَوالَيْنا وَلا عَلَيْنا،
اللّهُمَّ عَلى الآكامِ وَالظِّراب، 
وَبُطونِ الأوْدِية، وَمَنابِتِ الشَّجر
items.en:
O Allah, let the rain fall around us and not upon us, 
O Allah, (let it fall) on the pastures, hills, valleys, and the roots of trees.
items.tr:
Allāhumma ḥawālaynā wa lā `alaynā. 
Allāhumma `ala ‘l-ākāmi waẓ-ẓirāb, 
wa buṭūni ‘l-awdiyati, wa manābitish-shajar.
items.ref: Al-Bukhari 1/224, Muslim 1/614
ti: O Allah, let the rain fall around …

cats.en: Invocation for sighting the new moon

items.ar:
اللهُ أَكْبَر،
اللّهُمَّ أَهِلَّهُ عَلَيْنا بِالأمْنِ وَالإيمان،
والسَّلامَةِ والإسْلام،
وَالتَّوْفيقِ لِما تُحِبُّ رَبَّنا وَتَرْضى، 
رَبُّنا وَرَبُّكَ الله
items.en:
Allah is the Most Great. 
O Allah, bring us the new moon with security and Faith, 
with peace and in Islam, 
and in harmony with what our Lord loves and what pleases Him. 
Our Lord and your Lord is Allah.
items.tr:
Allāhu Akbar, 
Allāhumma ahillahu `alayna bi ‘l-amni wa ‘l-īmān,
was-salāmati wa ‘l-'Islām, 
wat-tawfīqi limā tuḥibbu Rabbanā wa tarḍā, 
Rabbunā wa Rabbukallāh.
items.ref: At-Tirmidhi 5/504, Ad-Darimi 1/336. See also Al-Albani, Sahih At-Tirmidhi 3/157.
ti: Allah is the Most Great. O Allah, …

cats.en: Invocations for breaking the fast

items.ar:
ذَهَبَ الظَّمَأُ،
وَابْتَلَّتِ العُروق،
وَثَبَتَ الأجْرُ إِنْ شاءَ الله
items.en:
The thirst is gone,
the veins are moistened, 
and the reward is confirmed, if Allah wills.
items.tr:
Dhahabaẓ-ẓama', 
wabtallati ‘l-`urūq, 
wa thabata ‘l-'ajru in shā Allāh.
items.ref: Abu Dawud 2/306 and others. See also Al- Albani, Sahihul-Jami' As-Saghir 4/209.

cats.en: Invocations before eating

items.ar:
إِذَا أَكَلَ أَحَدُكُمْ طَعَاماً فَلْيَقُلْ 
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ،
فَإِنْ نَسِيَ فِي أَوَّلِهِ فَلْيَقُلْ 
بسمِ اللَّهِ فِي أَوَّلِهِ وَآخِرِهِ
items.en:
When anyone of you begins eating, say:

With the Name of Allah.

And if you forget then, when you remember, say:

With the Name of Allah, in the beginning, and in the end.
items.tr:
When anyone of you begins eating, say: Bismillāh.
And if you forget then when you remember, say:
Bismillāhi fī awwalihi wa ākhirih.
items.ref: Abu Dawud 3/347, At-Tirmidhi 4/288. See Al- Albani's Sahih At-Tirmidhi 2/167.
ti: When anyone of you begins eating, say: …

items.ar:
مَنْ أَطْعَمَهُ اللَّهُ الطَّعَامَ فَلْيَقُلْ:
"اللَّهُمَّ بَارِكْ لَنَا فِيهِ
وَأَطْعِمْنَا خَيْراً مِنْهُ"،
 
وَمَنْ سَقَاهُ اللَّهُ لَبَناً فَلْيَقُلْ
"اللَّهُمَّ بَارِكْ لَنَا فِيهِ
وَزِدْنَا مِنْهُ"
items.en:
Whomever Allah has given food, should say:

O Allah, bless us in it and provide us with better than it.

Whomever Allah has given milk to drink, should say :

O Allah, bless us in it and give us more of it.
items.tr:
Whomever Allah has given food, should say: Allāhumma bārik lanā fīhi,
wa aṭ`imnā khayran minh.

Whomever Allah has given milk to drink, should say :
Allāhumma bārik lanā fīhi,
wa zidnā minh.
items.ref: At-Tirmidhi 5/506. See also Al-Albani, Sahih At-Tirmidhi 3/158.
ti: Whomever Allah has given food, should say: …

cats.en: Invocations after eating

items.ar:
الْحَمْدُ للهِ الَّذي أَطْعَمَني هذا
وَرَزَقَنيهِ مِنْ غَيْرِ حَوْلٍ مِنِّي وَلا قُوَّة
items.en:
Praise is to Allah Who has given me this food, 
and sustained me with it though I was unable to do it and powerless.
items.tr:
Alhamdu lillāhi ‘l-ladhī aṭ`amanī hādhā, 
wa razaqanīhi min ghayri ḥawlin minnī wa lā quwwah.
items.ref: At-Tirmidhi, Abu Dawud, and Ibn Majah. See also Al-Albani, Sahih At-Tirmidhi 3/159.
ti: Praise is to Allah Who has given …

items.ar:
الْحَمْدُ للهِ حَمْداً كَثيراً طَيِّباً مُبارَكاً فيه،
غَيْرَ مَكْفِيٍّ وَلا مُوَدَّعٍ وَلا مُسْتَغْنىً عَنْهُ رَبَّنا
items.en: All praise is to Allah, praise in abundance, good and blessed. It cannot [be compensated for, nor can it] be left, nor can it be done without, our Lord.
items.tr:
Alhamdu lillāhi ḥamdan kathīran tayyiban mubārakan fīh, 
ghayra makfiyyin wa lā muwadda`in, 
wa lā mustaghnan `anhu Rabbanā.
items.ref: Al-Bukhari 6/214, At-Tirmidhi 5/507.
ti: All praise is to Allah, praise in …

cats.en: A dinner guest's invocation for his host

items.ar:
اللّهُمَّ بارِكْ لَهُمْ فيما رَزَقْتَهُم، 
وَاغْفِرْ لَهُمْ وَارْحَمْهُمْ
items.en:
O Allah, bless them in what You have provided for them, 
and forgive them and have mercy on them.
items.tr:
Allāhumma bārik lahum fī mā razaqtahum, 
wagh’fir lahum warḥamhum.
items.ref: Muslim 3/1615.
ti: O Allah, bless them in what You …

cats.en: Invocation for someone who gives you drink or offers it to you
cats.ar: التعريض بالدعاء لطلب الطعام أو الشراب

items.ar:
اللّهُمَّ أَطْعِمْ مَن أَطْعَمَني، 
وَاسْقِ مَن سقاني
items.en:
O Allah, feed the one who has fed me,
and give drink to the one who has given me drink.
items.tr:
Allāhumma aṭ`im man aṭ`amanī 
wasqi man saqānī.
items.ref: Muslim 3/126.
ti: O Allah, feed the one who has …

cats.en: Invocation for a family who invites you to break your fast with them
cats.ar: الدعاء إذا أفطر عند أهل بيت

items.ar:
أَفْطَرَ عِنْدَكُم الصّائِمونَ
وَأَكَلَ طَعامَكُمُ الأبْرار،
وَصَلَّتْ عَلَيْكُمُ الملائِكَة
items.en:
With you, those who are fasting have broken their fast, 
you have fed those who are righteous, 
and the angels recite their prayers upon you.
items.tr:
Afṭara `indakumuṣ-ṣā'imūn, 
wa akala ṭa`āmakumu ‘l-'abrār, 
wa ṣallat `alaykumu ‘l-malā'ikah.
items.ref: Abu Dawud 3/367, Ibn Majah 1/556, An-Nasa'i, 'Amalul-Yawm wal-Laylah 296-8. Al-Albani graded it authentic in Sahih Abu Dawud 2/730.
ti: With you, those who are fasting have …

cats.en: Invocation for someone who offers you food when you are fasting, which you decline
cats.ar: دعاء الصائم إذا حضر الطعام ولم يفطر

items.ar: (إِذَا دُعِيَ أَحَدُكُمْ فَلْيُجِبْ، فَإِنْ كَانَ صَائِماً فَلْيُصَلِّ، وَإِنْ كَانَ مُفْطِراً فَلْيَطْعَمْ)، وَمَعْنَى فَلْيُصَلِّ أَيْ فَلْيَدْعُ.
items.en:
When you are invited (to eat) then reply to the invitation. 
If you are fasting then invoke Allah's blessings (on your host), 
and if you are not fasting then eat.
items.ref: Muslim 2/1054.

cats.en: What to say when you are fasting and someone is rude to you
cats.ar: ما يقول الصائم إذا سابه أحد

items.ar:
إِنِّي صَائِمٌ، 
إِنِّي صَائِمٌ
items.en:
I am fasting. 
I am fasting.
items.tr:
Innī ṣā'im,
innī ṣā'im.
items.ref: Al-Bukhari, cf. Al-Asqalani, Fathul-BAri 4/103, Muslim 2/806.

cats.en: Invocation for when you see the first dates of the season

items.ar:
اللّهُمَّ بارِكْ لَنا في ثَمَرِنا،
وَبارِكْ لَنا في مَدينَتِنا،
وَبارِكْ لَنا في صاعِنا،
وَبارِكْ لَنا في مُدِّنا
items.en:
O Allah, bless us in our dates and bless us in our town, 
bless us in our Sa' and in our Mudd.
items.tr:
Allahumma bārik lanā fī thamarinā, 
wa bārik lanā fī madīnatinā 
wa bārik lanā fī ṣā`inā, 
wa bārik lanā fī muddinā.
items.ref: Muslim 2/1000 (Sa' and Mudd are both dry measures used for agricultural produce by the Arabs in the Prophet's time. Of the two, the So.' was the larger measure.) (Translator)
ti: O Allah, bless us in our dates …

cats.en: Invocation for sneezing

items.ar: إِذَا عَطَسَ أَحَدُكُم فَلْيَقُلِ (الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ)، وَلْيَقُلْ لَهُ أَخُوهُ أَوْ صَاحِبُهُ: (يَرْحَمُكَ اللَّهُ)، فَإِذَا قَالَ لَهُ: (يَرحَمُكَ اللَّهُ)، فَلْيَقُلْ: (يَهْدِيكُمُ اللَّهُ وَيُصْلِحُ بَالَكُمْ)
items.en:
When you sneeze, then say:
All praises and thanks are to Allah.

Your companion should say:
May Allah have mercy upon you.

When someone says Yarḥamukallāh to you then you should say:
May Allah guide you and set your affairs in order.
items.tr:
When you sneeze , then say : Alḥamdulillāh

Your companion should say :
Yarḥamukallāh

When someone says Yarḥamukallāh to you then you should say:
Yahdīkumu ‘llāhu wa yuṣliḥu bālakum.
items.ref: Al-Bukhari 7/125.
ti: When you sneeze, then say: All praises …

cats.ar: ما يقال للكافر إذا عطس فحمد الله

items.ar: يَهْديكُمُ اللهُ وَيُصْلِحُ بالَكُم
items.en: May Allah guide you and set your affairs in order
items.tr: Yahdīkumullāhu wa yuṣliḥu bālakum.
items.ref: At-Tirmidhi 5/82, Ahmad 4/400, Abu Dawud 4/ 308. See also Al-Albani, Sahih At-Tirmidhi 2/354.

cats.en: Invocation for the groom

items.ar:
بارَكَ اللّهُ لَك، 
وَبارَكَ عَلَيْك، 
وَجَمَعَ بَيْنَكُما في خَيْر
items.en:
May Allah bless you,
and shower His blessings upon you, 
and join you together in goodness.
items.tr:
Bārakallāhu lak, 
wa bāraka `alayk, 
wa jama`a baynakumā fī khayr.
items.ref: Abu Dawud, Ibn Majah and At-Tirmidhi. See also Al-Albani, Sahih At-Tirmidhi 1/316.

cats.en: The groom’s supplication on the wedding night or when buying an animal

items.ar:
إِذَا تَزَوَّجَ أَحَدُكُمُ امْرَأَةً، أَوْ إِذَا اشْتَرَى خَادِماً فَلْيَقُلْ: 
(اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ خَيْرَهَا، 
وَخَيْرَ مَا جَبَلْتَهَا عَلَيْهِ، 
وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّهَا، 
وَشَرِّ مَا جَبَلْتَهَا عَلَيْهِ)، 
وَإِذَا اشْتَرَى بَعِيراً فَلْيَأْخُذْ بِذِرْوَةِ سَنَامِهِ وَلْيَقُلْ مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ.
items.en:
When any of you marries a woman or purchases a maid-servant then let him say :

O Allah, I ask You for the goodness of her,
and the goodness upon which You have created her,
and I seek refuge in You from the evil of her, 
and from the evil upon which You have created her.

If you purchase a camel then take hold of the top of its hump and say the same.
items.tr:
When any of you marries a woman or purchases a maid-servant then let him say: Allāhumma innī as'aluka khayrahā 
wa khayra mā jabaltahā `alayh,
wa a`ūdhu bika min sharrihā 
wa sharri mā jabaltahā `alayh.
items.ref: Abu Dawud 2/248 and Ibn Majah 1/617. See also Al-Albani, Sahih Ibn Majah 1/324.
ti: When any of you marries a woman …

cats.en: Invocation to be recited before intercourse

items.ar:
بِسْمِ الله 
اللّهُمَّ جَنِّبْنا الشَّيْطانَ، 
وَجَنِّبِ الشَّيْطانَ ما رَزَقْتَنا
items.en:
With the Name of Allah. 
O Allah, keep the Devil away from us, 
and keep the Devil away from that which You provide for us.
items.tr:
Bismillāh. 
Allāhumma jannibnash-Shayṭān, 
wa jannibish-Shayṭāna mā razaqtanā.
items.ref: Al-Bukhari 6/141, Muslim 2/1028.
ti: With the Name of Allah. O Allah, …

cats.en: Invocation for anger

items.ar: أَعوذُ بِاللهِ مِنَ الشَّيْطانِ الرَّجيم
items.en: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the outcast.
items.tr: A`ūdhu billāhi minash-Shayṭānir-rajīm.
items.ref: Al-Bukhari 7/99, Muslim 4/2015.
ti: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan …

cats.en: What to say if you see someone afflicted by misfortune

items.ar:
الْحَمْدُ للهِ الّذي عافاني مِمّا ابْتَلاكَ بِهِ،
وَفَضَّلَني عَلى كَثيرٍ مِمَّنْ خَلَقَ تَفْضيلا
items.en:
Praise is to Allah Who has spared me what He has afflicted you with, 
and preferred me greatly above much of what He has created.
items.tr:
Alhamdu lillāhi ‘l-ladhī `āfānī mimmab-talāka bihi 
wa faḍḍalanī `alā kathīrin mimman khalaqa tafḍīlā.
items.ref: At-Tirmidhi 5/493,4. See also Al-Albani, Sahih At-Tirmidhi 3/153.
ti: Praise is to Allah Who has spared …

cats.en: What to say while sitting in an assembly

items.ar:
عن ابن عمر قال: كان يعد لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في المجلس الواحد مائة مرة من قبل أن يقوم 
"رب اغفر لي 
وتب علي 
إنك أنت التواب الغفور"
items.en:
Ibn Umar (ra) said: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) used to repeat in a single sitting:

My Lord, forgive me,
and accept my repentance, 
You are the Ever-Relenting, the All-Forgiving.
items.tr:
Ibn Umar (ra) said: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) used to repeat in a single sitting:
Rabbigh’fir lī 
wa tub `alayy 
innaka antat-Tawwābu ‘l-Ghafūr.
items.ref: Sahih Ibn Majah 2/321. See also Al-Albani, Sahih At-Tirmidhi 3/153.

cats.en: The Expiation of Assembly - Kaffaratul-Majlis

items.ar:
سُبْحانَكَ اللّهُمَّ وَبِحَمدِك، 
أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لا إِلهَ إِلاّ أَنْتَ 
أَسْتَغْفِرُكَ وَأَتوبُ إِلَيْك
items.en:
Glory is to You, O Allah, and praise is to You. 
I bear witness that there is none worthy of worship but You. 
I seek Your forgiveness and repent to You.
items.tr:
Subhānaka Allāhumma wa biḥamdik, 
ash-hadu an lā ilāha illā ant,
astaghfiruka wa atību ilayk.
items.ref: Abu Dawud, Ibn Majah, At-Tirmidhi and An-Nasa'i. See also Al-Albani, Sahih At-Tirmidhi 3/ 153. Aishah (RA) said: "Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) did not sit in a gathering, and did not recite the Qur'an, and did not perform any prayer without concluding by saying ... (then she quoted the above)." This was reported by An-Nasa'i in 'Amalul-Yawm wal-Laylah (no.308), and Dr. Farooq Hamadah graded it authentic in his checking of t
ti: Glory is to You, O Allah, and …

items.en: May Allah reward you with good.

cats.en: Invocation for Allah's protection from the False Messiah
cats.ar: ما يعصم الله به من الدجال

items.ar: .(مَنْ حَفِظَ عَشْرَ آيَاتٍ مِنْ أَوَّلِ سُورَةِ الْكَهْفِ عُصِمَ مِنَ الدَّجَّالِ)، وَالْاسْتِعَاذَةُ بِاللَّهِ مِنْ فِتْنَتِهِ عَقِبَ التَّشَهُّدِ الْأَخِيرِ مِنْ كُلِّ صَلاَةٍ.
items.en:
Whoever memorizes ten 'Ayat (Verses) from the beginning of Surat Al-Kahf, will be protected from the False Messiah 
if he recites in every prayer after the final Tashahhud before ending the prayer, seeking the protection of Allah from the trials of the False Messiah.
items.ref: 1 Muslim 1/555, another version mentions the last ten 'Ayat, Muslim 1/556. 2 See invocations no. 55 and 56 of this book.

cats.en: Invocation for someone who tells you I love you for the sake of Allah
cats.ar: الدعاء لمن قال إني أحبك في الله

items.ar: أَحَبَّكَ الّذي أَحْبَبْتَني لَه
items.en: May He for Whose sake you love me, love you.
items.tr: Aḥabbaka ‘lladhī aḥbabtanī lah.
items.ref: Abu Dawud 4/333. Al-Albani graded it good in Sahih Abu Dawud 3/965.
ti: May He for Whose sake you love …

cats.en: Invocation for someone who offers you a share of his wealth

items.ar: بارَكَ اللهُ لَكَ في أَهْلِكَ وَمالِك
items.en: May Allah bless you in your family and your property.
items.tr: Bārakallāhu laka fī ahlika wa mālik.
items.ref: Al-Bukhari, cf. Al-Asqalani, Fathul-BAri 4/88.
ti: May Allah bless you in your family …

cats.en: Invocation (upon receipt of the loan) for someone who lends you money

items.ar:
بارَكَ اللهُ لَكَ في أَهْلِكَ وَمالِك، 
إِنَّما جَزاءُ السَّلَفِ الْحَمْدُ والأَداء
items.en:
May Allah bless you in your family and your wealth, 
surely the reward for a loan is praise and returning (what was borrowed).
items.tr:
Bārakallāhu laka fī ahlika wa mālik, 
innamā jazā'us-salafi ‘l-ḥamdu wa‘l-adā'.
items.ref: An-Nasa'i, 'Amalul-Yawm wal-Laylahp. 300, Ibn Majah 2/809. See also Al-Albani, Sahih Ibn Majah2/55.
ti: May Allah bless you in your family …

cats.en: Invocation for fear of Shirk

items.ar:
اللّهُمَّ إِنّي أَعوذُبِكَ أَنْ أُشْرِكَ بِكَ وَأَنا أَعْلَمْ، 
وَأَسْتَغْفِرُكَ لِما لا أَعْلَم
items.en:
O Allah, I seek refuge in You lest I associate anything with You knowingly, 
and I seek Your forgiveness for what I know not.
items.tr:
Allāhumma innī a`ūdhu bika an ushrika bika wa anā a`lam, 
wa astaghfiruka limā lā a`lam.
items.ref: Ahmad 4/403. See also Al-Albani, Sahihul-Jami' As-Saghir 3/233 and Sahihut-Targhib wat- Tarhib 1/19.
ti: O Allah, I seek refuge in You …

cats.en: Invocation against evil portent

items.ar:
اللّهُمَّ لا طَيْرَ إِلاّ طَيْرُك، 
وَلا خَيْرَ إِلاّ خَيْرُك، 
وَلا إِلهَ غَيْرُك
items.en:
O Allah there is no portent other than Your portent, 
no goodness other than Your goodness, 
and none worthy of worship other than You.
items.tr:
Allāhumma lā ṭayra illā ṭayruk, 
wa lā khayra illā khayruk, 
wa lā ilāha ghayruk.
items.ref: Ahmad 2/220, Ibn As-Sunni (no. 292). See also Al-Albani, Silsilatul-'Ahadlth As-Sahihah 3/54, (no. 1065). As for bodings of good, these used to please the Prophet (ﷺ) and so when he heard good words from someone, he used to say: "We have taken from you a good portent from your mouth," Abu Dawud, Ahmad. See also Al-Albani, Silsilatul-'Ahadith As-Sahihah 2/363, and it is with Abu Ash-Shaikh Al-Asfahani in 'Akhlaqun-Nab
ti: O Allah there is no portent other …

cats.en: Invocation for riding in a vehicle or on an animal

items.ar:
بِسْمِ اللهِ
وَالْحَمْدُ لله،
﴿سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي سَخَّرَ لَنَا هَذَا وَمَا كُنَّا لَهُ مُقْرِنِينَ *
وَإِنَّا إِلَى رَبِّنَا لَمُنقَلِبُونَ﴾
الحَمْدُ لله، الحَمْدُ لله، الحَمْدُ لله،
اللهُ أكْبَر، اللهُ أكْبَر، اللهُ أكْبَر، 
سُبْحانَكَ اللّهُمَّ إِنّي ظَلَمْتُ نَفْسي
فَاغْفِرْ لي،
فَإِنَّهُ لا يَغْفِرُ الذُّنوبَ إِلاّ أَنْت
items.en:
With the Name of Allah. 
Praise is to Allah. 
Glory is to Him Who has provided this for us
though we could never have had it by our efforts. 
Surely, unto our Lord, we are returning.
Praise is to Allah. Praise is to Allah. Praise is to Allah. 
Allah is the Most Great. Allah is the Most 
Great. Allah is the Most Great. 
Glory is to You. O Allah, I have wronged my own soul. 
Forgive me, 
for surely none forgives sins but You.
items.tr:
Bismillāh, 
walḥamdulillāh. 
Subḥāna ‘lladhī sakhkhara lanā hādhā
wa mā kunnā lahu muqrinīn. 
Wa innā ilā Rabbinā lamunqalibūn. 
Alḥamdulillāh, alḥamdulillāh, alḥamdulillāh, 
Allāhu Akbar, Allāhu Akbar, Allāhu Akbar, 
Subḥānaka ‘llāhumma innī ẓalamtu nafsī, 
faghfir lī, 
fa innahu lā yaghfirudh-dhunūba illā ant.
items.ref: Abu Dawud 3/34, At-Tirmidhi 5/501. See also Al-Albani, Sahih At-Tirmidhi3/156.
ti: With the Name of Allah. Praise is …

cats.en: Invocation for traveling

items.ar:
"اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ،
﴿سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي سَخَّرَ لَنَا هَذَا وَمَا كُنَّا لَهُ مُقْرِنِينَ *
وَإِنَّا إِلَى رَبِّنَا لَمُنقَلِبُونَ﴾
اللَّهُمَّ إِنّا نَسْأَلُكَ فِي سَفَرِنَا هَذَا البِرَّ وَالتَّقْوَى،
وَمِنَ الْعَمَلِ مَا تَرْضَى،
اللَّهُمَّ هَوِّنْ عَلَيْنَا سَفَرَنَا هَذَا
وَاطْوِ عَنَّا بُعْدَهُ،
اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ الصَّاحِبُ فِي السَّفَرِ،
وَالْخَليفَةُ فِي الْأَهْلِ،
اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ وَعْثَاءِ السَّفَرِ،
وَكَآبَةِ الْمَنْظَرِ،
وَسُوءِ الْمُنْقَلَبِ فِي الْمَالِ وَالْأَهْلِ"،
 وإذا رَجَعَ قَالَهُنَّ وَزَادَ فِيهِنَّ:
"آيِبُونَ، تائِبُونَ، عَابِدُونَ،
لِرَبِّنَا حَامِدُونَ".
items.en:
Allah is the Most Great. Allah is the Most Great. Allah is the Most Great. 
Glory is to Him Who has provided this for us
though we could never have had it by our efforts. 
Surely, unto our Lord we are returning. 
O Allah, we ask You on this our journey for goodness and piety, 
and for works that are pleasing to You. 
O Allah, lighten this journey for us
and make its distance easy for us. 
O Allah, You are our Companion on the road
and the One in Whose care we leave our family. 
O Allah, I seek refuge in You from this journey's hardships,
and from the wicked sights in store 
and from finding our family and property in misfortune upon returning.

(Upon returning recite the same again adding :)

We return repentant to our Lord, worshipping our Lord,
and praising our Lord.
items.tr:
Allāhu Akbar, Allāhu Akbar, Allāhu Akbar, 
Subḥāna ‘l-ladhi sakhkhara lanā hādhā 
wa mā kunnā lahu muqrinīn. 
Wa innā ilā Rabbinā lamunqalibūn. 
Allāhumma innā nas'aluka fī safarinā hādha ‘l-birra wat-taqwā, 
Wa mina ‘l-`amali mā tarḍā, 
Allāhumma hawwin `alaynā safaranā hādhā
waṭwi `annā bu`dah, 
Allāhumma antas-sāḥibu fis-safar, 
wa ‘l-khalīfatu fil-ahl, 
Allāhumma innī a`ūdhu bika min wa`thā'is-safar, 
wa ka'ābati ‘l-manẓar, 
wa sū'il-munqalabi fil-māli wa ‘l-ahl.

(Upon returning recite the same again adding): Ā’ibūna, tā'ibūna, `ābidūn, 
Li Rabbinā ḥāmidūn.
items.ref: Muslim 2/978.
ti: Allah is the Most Great. Allah is …

cats.en: Invocation for entering a town or city

items.ar:
أللّهُمَّ رَبَّ السَّمواتِ السّبْعِ وَما أَظْلَلَن،
وَرَبَّ الأَراضينَ السّبْعِ وَما أقْلَلْن،
وَرَبَّ الشَّياطينِ وَما أَضْلَلْن،
وَرَبَّ الرِّياحِ وَما ذَرَيْن،
أَسْأَلُكَ خَيْرَ هذهِ الْقَرْيَةِ
وَخَيْرَ أَهْلِها،
وَخَيْرَ ما فيها،
وَأَعوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّها
وَشَرِّ أَهْلِها،
وَشَرِّ ما فيها
items.en:
O Allah, Lord of the seven heavens and all they overshadow,
Lord of the seven worlds and all they uphold, 
Lord of the devils and all they lead astray,
Lord of the winds and all they scatter. 
I ask You for the goodness of this town, 
and for the goodness of its people, 
and for the goodness it contains. 
I seek refuge in You from its evil, 
from the evil of its people, 
and from the evil it contains.
items.tr:
Allāhumma Rabbas-samāwātis-sab`i wa mā aẓlaln, 
Wa Rabba ‘l-arāḍīnas-sab`i wa mā aqlaln, 
wa Rabbash-shayāṭīni wa mā aḍlaln, 
wa Rabbar-riyāḥi wa mā dharayn. 
As'aluka khayra hādhihi ‘l-qaryah, 
wa khayra ahlihā, 
wa khayra māfīhā, 
wa a`ūdhu bika min sharrihā, 
wa sharri ahlihā, 
wa sharri mā fīhā.
items.ref: Al-Hakim who graded it authentic and Ath-Tfaahabi agreed 2/100, and Ibn As-Sunni (no. 524). Al-Hafidh graded it good in his checking of Al-'Athkdr 5/154. Ibn Baz said in Tuhfatul-'Akhydr p. 37, that An-Nasa'i recorded it with a good chain of narration.
ti: O Allah, Lord of the seven heavens …

cats.en: Invocation for entering a market

items.ar:
لا إلهَ إلاّ اللّه
وحدَهُ لا شريكَ لهُ،
لهُ المُلْكُ ولهُ الحَمْد، 
يُحْيي وَيُميتُ
وَهُوَ حَيٌّ لا يَموت،
بِيَدِهِ الْخَيْرُ
وَهوَ على كلّ شيءٍ قدير
items.en:
None has the right to be worshipped but Allah alone, 
Who has no partner.
His is the dominion and His is the praise. He brings life and He causes death, 
and He is living and does not die. 
In His Hand is all good, 
and He is Able to do all things.
items.tr:
Lā ilāha illallāh
waḥdahu lā sharīka lah, 
Lahu ‘l-mulku wa lahu ‘l-ḥamd, 
Yuḥyī wa yumīt, 
wa huwa ḥayyun lā yamūt,
Biyadihi ‘l-khayr, 
wa huwa `alā kulli shay'in Qadīr.
items.ref: At-Tirmidhi 5/291, and Al-Hakim 1/538. Al-Albani graded it good in Sahih Ibn Majah 2/21 and Sahih At-Tirmidhi 3/152.
ti: None has the right to be worshipped …

cats.en: Invocation for when your vehicle or mount begins to fail

items.ar: بِسْمِ اللهِ
items.en: With the Name of Allah.
items.tr: Bismillāh.
items.ref: Abu Dawud 4/296. Al-Albani graded it authentic in Sahih Abu Dawud 3/941.

cats.en: The traveler's invocation for the one he leaves behind

items.ar: أَسْتَوْدِعُكُمُ اللَّهَ الَّذي لا تَضيعُ وَدائِعُه
items.en: I place you in the trust of Allah, whose trust is never misplaced.
items.tr: Astawdi`ukumu ‘llāha ‘l-ladhi lā taḍī`u wadā'i`uh.
items.ref: Ahmad 2/403, Ibn Majah 2/943. See also Al-Albani, Sahih Ibn Majah 2/133.
ti: I place you in the trust of …

cats.en: The resident's invocations for the traveler

items.ar:
أَسْتَوْدِعُ اللَّهَ دينَكَ
وَأَمانَتَكَ، 
وَخَواتيمَ عَمَلِك
items.en:
I leave your religion in the care of Allah, 
as well as your safety, 
and the last of your deeds.
items.tr:
Astawdi`ullāha dīnak, 
wa amānatak, 
wa khawātīma `amalik.
items.ref: Ahmad 2/7, At-Tirmidhi 5/499. See also Al-Albani, Sahih At-Tirmidhi 2/155.
ti: I leave your religion in the care …

items.ar:
زَوَّدَكَ اللَّهُ التقْوى، 
وَغَفَرَذَنْبَكَ، 
وَيَسَّرَ لَكَ الخَيْرَ حَيْثُما كُنْت
items.en:
May Allah give you piety as your provision, 
forgive your sins, 
and make goodness easy for you wherever you are.
items.tr:
Zawwadaka ‘llāhut-taqwā, 
wa ghafara dhanbak, 
wa yassara laka ‘l-khayra ḥaythu mā kunt.
items.ref: At-Tirmidhi. See Al-Albani, Sahih At-Tirmidhi, 3/155.

cats.en: Glorifying and magnifying Allah on the journey
cats.ar: التكبير و التسبيح في سير السفر

items.ar:
قَالَ جَابِرٌ رضي الله عنه: 
(كُنَّا إِذَا صَعَدْنَا كَبَّرْنَا، 
وَإِذَا نَزَلْنَا سَبَّحْنَا)
items.en:
Jabir (ra), said: Whenever we went up a hill we would say 
Allāhu Akbar (Allah is the Most Great) 
and when we descended we would say 
Subḥānallāh (Glory is to Allah).
items.ref: Al-Bukhari, cf. Al-Asqalani, Fathul-Bari 6/135.
ti: Jabir (ra), said: Whenever we went up …

cats.en: The traveler's invocation at dawn

items.ar:
سَمِعَ سامِعٌ بِحَمْدِ اللهِ وَحُسْنِ بَلائِهِ عَلَيْنا.
رَبَّنا صاحِبْنا وَأَفْضِل عَلَيْنا 
عائِذاً باللهِ مِنَ النّار
items.en:
He Who listens has heard that we praise Allah for the good things He gives us. 
Our Lord, be with us and bestow Your favor upon us. 
I seek the protection of Allah from the Fire.
items.tr:
Sami`a sāmi`un biḥamdillāhi wa ḥusni balā'ihi `alaynā. 
Rabbanā ṣāḥibnā, wa afḍil `alaynā, 
`ā'idhan billāhi minan-nār.
items.ref: Muslim 4/2086, the meaning of sami`a sāmi`un (who listens has heard) is that 'a witness has witnessed our praise of Allah due to His blessings and favor upon us.' It could also be read samma`a sāmi`un, in which case it means 'one who has heard this statement of mine will convey it to another and he will say it as well.' This is due to the attention given to the Thikr (remembrance of Allah) and supplications made duri
ti: He Who listens has heard that we …

cats.en: Invocation for a layover (stopping along the way) on the journey
cats.ar: الدعاء إذا نزل مترلا في سفر أو غيره

items.ar: أَعوذُ بِكَلِماتِ اللّهِ التّامّاتِ مِنْ شَرِّ ما خَلَق
items.en: I seek refuge in the Perfect Words of Allah from the evil of what He has created.
items.tr: A`ūdhu bikalimāti ‘llāhit-tāmmāti min sharri mā khalaq.
items.ref: Muslim 4/2080.
ti: I seek refuge in the Perfect Words …

cats.en: What to say upon returning from a Journey

items.ar:
يُكَبِّرُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَرَفٍ ثَلاَثَ تَكْبِيرَاتٍ ثُمَّ يَقُولُ: 
لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ 
وَحْدَهُ لاَ شَرِيكَ لَهُ، 
لَهُ الْمُلْكُ، وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ، 
وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ، 
آيِبُونَ، تَائِبُونَ، عَابِدُونَ، 
لِرَبِّنا حَامِدُونَ، 
صَدَقَ اللَّهُ وَعْدَهُ، 
وَنَصَرَ عَبْدَهُ، 
وَهَزَمَ الْأَحْزابَ وَحْدَهُ
items.en:
From every elevated point say Allāhu Akbar (Allah is the Most Great) three times and then recite:

None has the right to be worshipped but Allah alone, 
Who has no partner. 
His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He is Able to do all things. 
We return repentant to our Lord, worshipping our Lord, 
and praising our Lord. 
He fulfilled His Promise, 
He aided His slave, 
and He alone defeated the Confederates.
items.tr:
From every elevated point say 
Allāhu Akbar (three times), 
and then recite: Lā ilāha illallāh 
waḥdahu lā sharīka lah, 
lahu ‘l-mulku, walahu ‘l-ḥamd, 
wa Huwa `alā kulli shay'in Qadīr, 
ā'ibūna, tā'ibūna,`ābidūn, 
li Rabbinā ḥāmidūn, 
sadaqallāhu wa`dah, 
wa nasara `abdah,
wa hazama ‘l-'aḥzāba waḥdah.
items.ref: Bukhari 7/163, Muslim 2/980. The Prophet (ﷺ) used to say this when returning from a campaign or from Hajj.
ti: From every elevated point say Allāhu Akbar …

cats.en: What to say if something happens to please you or to displease you
cats.ar: ما يقول من أتاه أمر يسره أو يكرهه

items.ar: كَانَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم إِذَا أَتَاهُ الْأَمْرُ يَسُرُّهُ قَالَ: (الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي بِنِعْمَتِهِ تَتِمُّ الصَّالِحَاتُ) وَإِذَا أَتَاهُ الْأَمْرُ يَكْرَهُهُ قَالَ: (الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ عَلَى كُلِّ حَالٍ)
items.en:
When something happened that pleased him, the Prophet (ﷺ) used to say:
Praise is to Allah Who by His blessings all good things are perfected.

And if something happened that displeased him, he used to say:
Praise is to Allah in all circumstances.
items.tr:
When something happened that pleased him, the Prophet (ﷺ) used to say: Alḥamdu lillāhi ‘lladhi bi ni`matihi tatimmuṣ-ṣāliḥāt.
And if something happened that displeased him, he used to say:
Alḥamdu lillāhi `alā kulli ḥāl.
items.ref: Ibn As-Sunni, 'Amalul-Yawm wal-Laylah, and Al-Hakim who graded it authentic 1/499. See also Al-Albani, Sahihul-Jami' As-Saghir 4/201.

cats.en: The excellence of asking for Allah's blessings upon the Prophet pbuh
cats.ar: فضل الصلاة على النبي صلى الله عليه و سلم

items.ar: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم: (مَنْ صَلَّى عَلَيَّ صَلاَةً صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ بِهَا عَشْراً)
items.en: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever prays for Allah's blessings upon me once, will be blessed for it by Allah ten times."
items.ref: Muslim 1/288.

items.ar: وَقَالَ صلى الله عليه وسلم: (لاَ تَجْعَلُوا قَبْرِي عِيداً وَصَلُّوا عَلَيَّ؛ فَإِنَّ صَلاَتَكُم تَبْلُغُنِي حَيْثُ كُنْتُمْ)
items.en: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Do not make my grave a place of ritual celebration, but pray for Allah's blessings upon me, for your blessings reach me from wherever you are.
items.ref: Abu Dawud 2/218, Ahmad 2/367. Al-Albani graded it authentic in Sahih Abu Dawud 2/383.

items.ar: وَقَالَ صلى الله عليه وسلم: (الْبَخِيلُ مَنْ ذُكِرْتُ عِنْدَهُ فَلَمْ يُصَلِّ عَلَيَّ)
items.en: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The miser is the one in whose presence I am mentioned yet does not pray for Allah's blessings upon me."
items.ref: At-Tirmidhi 5/551 and others. See also Al-Albani, Sahih At-Tirmidhi 3/177 and Sahihul-Jarai' As-Saghir 3/25.

items.ar: وَقَالَ صلى الله عليه وسلم:(إِنَّ لِلَّهِ مَلاَئِكَةً سَيَّاحِينَ فِي الْأَرْضِ يُبَلِّغُونِي مِنْ أُمَّتِي السَّلاَمَ)
items.en: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah has angels who roam the earth and they convey to me the greetings (or prayers of peace) of my Ummah (nation)."
items.ref: An-Nasa'i, Al-Hakim 2/421. Al-Albani graded it authentic in Sahih An-Nasa'i 1/274.

items.ar: وَقَالَ صلى الله عليه وسلم: (مَا مِنْ أَحَدٍ يُسَلِّمُ عَلَيَّ إِلاَّ رَدَّ اللَّهُ عَلَيَّ رُوحِيَ حَتَّى أَرُدَّ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمَ)
items.en: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "No one sends greetings (or prayers of peace) upon me but Allah returns my soul to me so that I may return his greetings."
items.ref: Abu Dawud (no. 2041). Al-Albani graded it good in Sahih Abu Dawud 1/383.

cats.en: Spreading the greetings of Salam (Peace)

items.ar: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم: (لاَ تَدْخُلُوا الْجَنَّةَ حَتَّى تُؤْمِنُوا، وَلاَ تُؤْمِنُوا حَتَّى تَحَابُّوا، أَوَلاَ أَدُلُّكُم عَلَى شَيْءٍ إِذَا فَعَلْتُمُوهُ تَحَابَبْتُم، أَفْشُوا السَّلاَمَ بَيْنَكُمْ)
items.en: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "You shall not enter Paradise until you believe, and you have not believed until you love one another. Shall I tell you of something you can do to make you love one another? Spread the greetings of Salam (peace) amongst yourselves (i.e. between each other).
items.ref: Muslim 1/74 and others.

items.ar: ثَلاَثٌ مَنْ جَمَعَهُنَّ فَقَدْ جَمَعَ الْإِيمَانَ: الْإِنْصَافُ مِنْ نَفْسِكَ، وَبَذْلُ السَّلاَمِ لِلْعَالَمِ، وَالْإِنْفَاقُ مِنَ الإِقْتَارِ
items.en: Three characteristics, whoever combines them, has completed his faith: to be just, to spread greetings to all people and to spend (charitably) out of the little you have.
items.ref: Al-Bukhari, cf. Al-Asqalani, Fathul-Bari 1/82 as a statement of the Companion 'Ammar (RA).
ti: Three characteristics, whoever combines them, has completed …

items.ar: وَعَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عُمَرَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا: أنَّ رَجُلاً سَأَلَ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم أيُّ الْإِسْلاَمِ خَيْرٌ قَالَ: (تُطْعِمُ الطَّعَامَ، وَتَقْرأُ السَّلاَمَ عَلَى مَنْ عَرَفْتَ وَمَنْ لَمْ تَعْرِفْ)
items.en: `Abdullah bin `Umar (RA) said: A man asked the Prophet (ﷺ), "What is the best act of Islam?" He said, "To feed others and to give greetings of Salam (peace) to those whom you know and to those whom you do not know. "
items.ref: Al-Bukhari, cf. Al-Asqalani, Fathul-Bari 1/55, Muslim 1/65.

cats.en: How to reply to a disbeliever if he says Salam to you
cats.ar: كيف يرد السلام على الكافر إذا سلم

items.ar: إذَا سَلَّمَ عَلَيْكُمْ أَهْلُ الْكِتَابِ فَقُولُوا: وَعَلَيْكُمْ
items.en:
If one of the People of the Scripture (i.e. Christians and Jews) greets you saying As-Salaamu `alaykum, then say (to him):

And upon you .
items.tr: If one of the People of the Scripture (i.e. Christians and Jews) greets you, saying As-Salāmu `alaykum, then say (to him): Wa `alaykum.
items.ref: Al-Bukhari, cf. Al-Asqalani, Fathul-Bari 11/42, Muslim 4/1705.

cats.en: Invocation upon hearing the cock's crow or the bray of a donkey
cats.ar: الدُّعاءُ عِنْدَ سَمَاعِ صِياحِ الدِّيكِ ونَهِيقِ الْحِمَارِ

items.ar: إِذَا سَمِعْتُمْ صِيَاحَ الدِّيَكَةِ فَاسْأَلُوا اللَّهَ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ؛ فَإِنَّهَا رَأَتْ مَلَكاً وَإِذَا سَمِعْتُمْ نَهِيقَ الْحِمَارِ فَتَعَوَّذُوا بِاللَّهِ مِنَ الشَّيطَانِ؛ فَإِنَّهُ رَأَى شَيْطَاناً
items.en: When you hear the cock's crow, ask Allah for His favor upon you for surely it has seen an angel. When you hear the bray of a donkey, seek refuge in Allah from Satan, for surely it has seen a devil.
items.ref: Al-Bukhari, cf. Al-Asqalani, Fathul-Bari 6/350, Muslim 4/2092.

cats.en: Invocation upon hearing a dog barking in the night

items.ar: إِذَا سَمِعْتُمْ نُبَاحَ الْكِلاَبِ وَنَهِيقَ الْحَمِيرِ بِاللَّيْلِ فَتَعَوَّذُوا بِاللَّهِ مِنْهُنَّ؛ فَإِنَّهُنَّ يَرَيْنَ مَا لاَ تَرَوْنَ
items.en: When you hear a dog barking or a donkey braying in the night, then seek refuge in Allah from them, for surely they have seen what you see not.
items.ref: Abu Dawud 4/327, Ahmad 3/306. Al-Albani graded it authentic in Sahih Abu Dawud 3/961.

cats.en: Invocation for someone you have spoken ill to

items.ar: قال صلى الله عليه وسلم: "اللَّهُم فأيما مؤمن سببته فاجعل ذلك له قربة إليك يوم القيامة"
items.en: O Allah, whomever of the believers I have abused, give him the reward of a sacrificial slaughter for it on the Day of Resurrection.
items.tr:
Allāhumma fa'ayyumā mu'minin sababtuhu 
faj`al dhālika lahu qurbatan ilayka yawma ‘l-qiyāmah.
items.ref: Al-Bukhari, cf. Al-Asqalani, Fathul-Bari 11/171, Muslim 4/2007. The wording in Muslim's report is: 'make it a purification for him and a source of mercy.

cats.en: How a Muslim should praise another Muslim
cats.ar: ما يقول المسلم إذا مدح المسلم

items.ar: قال صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إِذَا كَانَ أَحَدُكُم مَادِحاً صَاحِبَهُ لاَ مَحَالَةَ فَلْيَقُلْ: أَحْسِبُ فُلاَناً وَاللَّهُ حَسِيبُهُ، وَلاَ أُزَكِّي عَلَى اللَّهِ أَحَداً، أَحْسِبُهُ – إِنْ كَانَ يَعْلَمُ ذَاكَ – كَذَا وَكَذَا"
items.en:
If any of you praises his companion then let him say:
I consider (such and such a person), and Allah is his Assessor, (meaning: and I cannot claim anyone to be pious before Allah) if you know of this (good character trait in the person) to be such and such (saying what he thinks is praiseworthy in that person).
items.tr:
If any of you praises his companion then let him say: Aḥsibu fulānan wallāhu ḥasībuh
wa lā uzakkī `alallāhi aḥada.
items.ref: Muslim 4/2296.

cats.en: What a Muslim should say when he is praised

items.ar: ((اللَّهُمَّ لاَ تُؤَاخِذْنِي بِمَا يَقُولُونَ، وَاغْفِرْ لِي مَا لاَ يَعْلَمُونَ، [وَاجْعَلْنِي خَيْراً مِمَّا يَظُّنُّونَ])).
items.en:
O Allah, do not call me to account for what they say
and forgive me for what they have no knowledge of 
[and make me better than they imagine].
items.tr:
Allāhumma lā tu'ākhidhnī bimā yaqūlūn, 
waghfir lī mā lā ya`lamūn
[waj`alnī khayran mimmā yaẓunnūn].
items.ref: Al-Bukhari, Al-'Adabul-Mufrad no. 761. See Al-Albani, Sahih Al-'Adabul-Mufrad (no. 585). The portion between brackets if from Al-Bayhaqi, Shu'ab Al-Iman 4/228, and comes another account.

cats.en: The pilgrim's announcement of his arrival for Hajj or Umrah
cats.ar: كيف يلبي المحرم في الحج أو العمرة ؟

items.ar:
لَبَّيْكَ اللَّهُمَّ لَبَّيْكَ، 
لَبَّيْكَ لاَ شَرِيكَ لَكَ لَبَّيْكَ، 
إِنَّ الْحَمْدَ والنِّعْمَة لَكَ والمُلْكُ، 
لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ
items.en:
I am here at Your service, O Allah, I am here at Your service. 
I am here at Your service, You have no partner, I am here at Your service. 
Surely the praise, and blessings are Yours, and the dominion. 
You have no partner.
items.tr:
Labbayk-Allāhumma labbayk, 
labbayka lā sharīka laka labbayk,
inna ‘l-ḥamda, wanni`mata, laka wa ‘l-mulk, 
lā sharīka lak.
items.ref: Al-Bukhari, cf. Al-Asqalani, Fathul-Bari 3/408, Muslim 2/841.

cats.en: Saying Allahu Akbar when passing the Black Stone

items.ar: طَافَ النَّبيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِالْبَيْتِ عَلَى بَعِيرٍ كُلَّمَا أَتَى الرُّكْنَ أَشَارَ إِلَيْهِ بِشَيْءٍ عِنْدَهُ وَكَبَّرَ
items.en: The Prophet (ﷺ) performed Tawaf riding a camel. Every time he passed the corner (containing the Black Stone), he would point to it with something that he was holding and say: Allāhu Akbar (Allah is the Most Great)!
items.ref: Al-Bukhari, cf. Al-Asqalani, Fathul-Bari 3/476. See also 472. The 'something' that was referred to in this Hadith was a cane.

cats.en: Invocation to be recited between the Yemenite Corner and the Black Stone

﴿رَبَّنَا آتِنَا في الدُّنْيَا حسَنَةً
وفي الآخِرَةِ حسَنةً 
وقِنَا عذَابَ النَّارِ﴾
items.en:
Our Lord, grant us the good things in this world,
and the good things in the next life,
and save us from the punishment of the Fire.

cats.en: Invocation to be recited while standing at Safa and Marwah

items.ar:
(لَمَّا دَنَا النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم مِنَ الصَّفَا قَرَأَ: ﴿إِنَّ الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةَ مِنْ شَعَآئِرِ اللَّهِ﴾ "أَبْدَأُ بِمَا بَدَأَ اللَّهُ بِهِ" فَبَدَأَ بِالصَّفَا فَرَقِيَ عَلَيْهِ حَتَّى رَأَى الْبَيْتَ، فَاسْتَقْبَلَ الْقِبْلَةَ، فَوَحَّدَ اللَّهَ وَكبَّرَهُ وَقَالَ: لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لاَ شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ، لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ، أَنْجَزَ وَعْدَهُ، وَنَصَرَ عَبْدَهُ، وَهَزَمَ الْأَحْزَابَ وَحْدَهُ، ثُمَّ دَعَا بَيْنَ ذلكَ. قَالَ مِثْلَ هَذَا ثَلاَثَ مَرَّاتٍ) الْحَدِيثُ.

 وَفِيهِ: (فَفَعَلَ عَلَى الْمَرْوَةِ كَمَا فَعَلَ عَلَى الصَّفَا)
items.en:
Whenever the Prophet (ﷺ) approached Mount Safa, he would recite:

Surely Safa and Marwah are among the signs of Allah. I begin by that which Allah began.

He began (his Sa'y) at Mount Safa climbing it until he could see the House. He then faced the Qiblah repeating the words:

There is none worthy of worship but Allah, and Allah is the Most Great.

Then he said:

None has the right to be worshipped but Allah alone, Who has no partner, His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He is Able to do all things. None has the right to be worshipped but Allah alone, He fulfilled His Promise, He aided His slave, and He alone defeated Confederates.

Then he would ask Allah for what he liked, repeating the same thing like this three times. He did at Mount Marwah as he did at Mount Safa.
items.tr:
Whenever the Prophet (ﷺ) approached Mount Safa, he would recite: Innaṣ-Ṣafā wa ‘l-Marwata min sha`ā'irillāh. 
Abda'u bimā bada'allāhu bih.
He began (his Sa`y) at Mount Safa climbing it, until he could see the House. He then faced the Qiblah repeating the words:
Lā ilāha illallāh, Allāhu Akbar
Then he said:
Lā ilāha 'illallāh
waḥdahu lā sharīka lah, 
Lahu ‘l-mulku wa lahu ‘l-ḥamd
wa Huwa `alā kulli shay'in Qadīr, 
lā 'ilāha illallāhu waḥdahu, 
anjaza wa`dahu, wa naṣara `abdahu, 
wa hazama ‘l 'aḥzāba waḥdah.
Then he would ask Allah for what he liked, repeating the same three times. He did at Mount Marwah as he did at Mount Safa.
items.ref: Muslim 2/888.

cats.en: Invocation to be recited on the Day of Arafat

items.ar:
خير الدعاء دعاء يوم عرفة، وخيرُ ما قلت أنا والنبيُّون من قبلي:
 
لا إله إلا الله وحدهُ
لا شريك لهُ،
لهُ الملكُ ولهُ الحمدُ
وهو على كل شيء قدير.
items.en:
None has the right to be worshipped but Allah 
Alone, Who has no partner. 
His is the dominion and His is the praise,
and He is Able to do all things.
items.tr:
Lā 'ilāha 'illallāhu 
waḥdahu lā sharīka lahu, 
lahul-mulku wa lahul-ḥamdu 
wa huwa `alā kulli shay'in qadīr.
items.ref: At-Tirmidhi. Al-Albani graded it good in Sahih At-Tirmidhi 3/184, and also Silsilatul-'Ahadith As-Sahihah 4/6.

items.ar: رَكِبَ صلى الله عليه وسلم الْقَصْوَاءَ حَتَّى أَتَى الْمَشْعَرَ الْحَرَامَ فَاسْتَقْبَلَ الْقِبْلَةَ (فَدَعَاهُ، وَكَبَّرَهُ، وَهَللَّهُ، وَوَحَّدَهُ) فَلَمْ يَزَلْ وَاقِفاً حَتَّى أَسْفَرَ جِدَّاً فَدَفَعَ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَطْلُعَ الشَّمسُ.
items.en: 'He (ﷺ) rode Al-Qaswa until he reached Al-MashAAar Al-Haram, he then faced the qiblah, supplicated to Allah, and extoled His greatness and oneness. He stood until the sun shone but left before it rose.'
items.ref: Muslim 2/891.

cats.en: Saying Allahu Akbar while stoning the three pillars at Mina
cats.ar: التكبير عند رمي الجمار مع كل حصاة

items.ar: يُكَبِّرُ كُلَّمَا رَمَى بِحَصَاةٍ عِنْدَ الْجِمَارِ الثَّلاَثِ، ثُمَّ يَتَقَدَّمُ، ويَقِفُ يَدْعُو مُسْتَقْبِلَ الْقِبلَةِ، رَافِعاً يَدَيْهِ بَعْدَ الْجَمْرَةِ الْأُولَى وَالثَّانِيَةِ. أَمَّا جَمْرَةُ الْعَقَبَةِ فَيَرْمِيهَا وَيُكَبِّرُ عِنْدَ كُلِّ حَصَاةٍ وَيَنْصَرِفُ وَلاَ يَقِفُ عِنْدَهَا
items.en: The Prophet (ﷺ) said Allāhu Akbar (Allah is the Most Great) with each pebble he threw at the three pillars. Then he went forward, stood facing the Qiblah, and raised his hands and called upon Allah. That was after (stoning) the first and second pillars. As for the third, he stoned it and called out Allāhu Akbar with every pebble he threw, but when he was finished he left without standing at it (for supplications).
items.ref: Al-Bukhari, cf. Al-Asqalani, Fathul-Bari 3/581, 3, 4, and Muslim

items.en: The Prophet (ﷺ), upon receiving news which pleased him or which caused pleasure, would prostrate in gratitude to Allah blessed and exalted.
items.ref: Abu Dawud, Ibn Majah, At-Tirmidhi. See also Al-Albani, Sahih Ibn Majah 1/233, and 'Irwa'ul-Ghalil 2/226.

cats.en: What to say when you feel a pain in your body
cats.ar: ما يقول من أحس وجعا في جسده

items.ar:
ضَعْ يَدَكَ عَلَى الَّذِي تَألَّمَ مِنْ جَسَدِكَ وَقُلْ:
"بِسْمِ اللَّهِ" ثَلاَثاً، 
وَقُلْ سَبْعَ مَرَّاتٍ: 
"أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ وَقُدْرَتِهِ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا أَجِدُ وَأُحَاذِرُ"
items.en:
Put your hand on the place where you feel pain and say:
With the Name of Allah (three times).

Then say seven times:
I seek refuge in Allah and in His Power from the evil of what I find and of what I guard against.
items.tr:
Put your hand on the place where you feel pain and say: Bismillāh (three times).
Then say seven times:
A`ūdhu billāhi wa qudratihi min sharri mā ajidu wa uḥādhir.
items.ref: Muslim 4/1728.

cats.en: What to say to foil the devil's plots
cats.ar: ما يقول لرد كيد مردة الشياطين

items.ar:
أَعُوذُ بكَلِمَاتِ اللهِ التَّامَّاتِ الَّتِي لَا يُجَاوِزُهُنَّ بَرٌّ ولَا فَاجرٌ 
مِنْ شّرِّ مَا خَلقَ، 
وبَرَأَ وذَرَأَ، 
ومِنْ شَرِّ مَا يَنْزِلُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ 
وِمنْ شَرِّ مَا يَعْرُجُ فيهَا، 
ومِن شَرِّ مَا ذَرَأَ في الأَرْضِ 
ومِنْ شَرِّ مَا يَخْرُجُ مِنْهَا، 
وِمنْ شَرِّ فِتَنِ اللَّيْلِ والنَّهارِ، 
ومِنْ شَرِّ كُلِّ طارِقٍ 
إِلَّا طَارِقاً يَطْرُقُ بخَيْرٍ 
يَا رَحْمَنُ
items.en:
I seek refuge in the Perfect Words of Allah -which neither the upright nor the corrupt may overcome -
from the evil of what He created, 
of what He made, and of what He scattered,
from the evil of what descends from the 
heavens, 
and of what rises up to them, 
from the evil of what He scattered in the earth, 
and of what emerges from it, 
from the evil trials of night and day, 
and from the evil of every night visitor,
except the night visitor who comes with good. 
O Merciful One.
items.tr:
A`ūdhu bikalimāti ‘llāhit-tāmmāti ‘llatī lā yujāwizuhunna barrun wa lā fājirun
min sharri mā khalaq, 
wa bara'a wa dhara', 
wa min sharri mā yanzilu minas-samā', 
wa min sharri mā ya`ruju fīhā, 
wa min sharri mā dhara'a fi ‘l-arḍ, 
wa min sharri ma yakhruju minhā, 
wa min sharri fitani ‘llayli wannahār, 
wa min sharri kulli ṭāriqin 
illā ṭāriqan yaṭruqu bikhayr 
yā Rahmān.
items.ref: Ahmad 3/419, with an authentic chain of narration, and Ibn As-Sunni (no. 637). Al-Arna'ut, graded its chain authentic in his checking of Al-'Aqidah At-Tahawiyyah p. 133. See also Majma'uz-Zawa'id, 10/127.

cats.en: Repentance and seeking forgiveness

items.ar: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم: "وَاللَّهِ إِنِّي لأَسْتَغفِرُ اللَّهَ وَأَتُوبُ إِلَيْهِ فِي الْيَوْمِ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ سَبْعِينَ مَرَّةٍ"
items.en: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: "By Allah, I seek the forgiveness of Allah, and repent to Him more than seventy times in a day.
items.ref: Al-Bukhari, cf. Al-Asqalani, Fathul-Bari 11/101.

items.ar: وَقَالَ صلى الله عليه وسلم: (يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ تُوبُوا إِلَى اللَّهِ فَإِنِّي أَتُوبُ فِي الْيَوْمِ إِلَيْهِ مِائَةَ مَرَّةٍ)
items.en: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: "O people, repent to Allah, for I verily repent to Him one hundred times a day.
items.ref: Muslim 4/2076.

items.ar: وَقَالَ صلى الله عليه وسلم: مَنْ قَالَ (أَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ الْعَظيمَ الَّذِي لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ هُوَ الْحَيُّ القَيّوُمُ وَأَتُوبُ إِلَيهِ)، غَفَرَ اللَّهُ لَهُ وَإِنْ كَانَ فَرَّ مِنَ الزَّحْفِ.
items.en:
Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: Whoever says:

I seek the forgiveness of Allah the Mighty, Whom there is none worthy of worship except Him, the Living, the Eternal, 
and I repent to Him, 
Allah will forgive him even if he has deserted the army's ranks.
items.tr:
Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: Whoever says:
Astaghfirullāha ‘l-'Aẓīm
alladhi lā ilāha illā huwa ‘l-ḥayyul-Qayyūm 
wa atūbu ilayh.
items.ref: Abu Dawud 2/85, At-Tirmidhi 5/569, and Al-Hakim who declared it authentic and Ath-Thahabi agreed with him 1/511. Al-Albani graded it authentic in Sahih At-Tirmidhi 3/182. See also Jami'ul-'Usool li-'Ahdaith Ar-Rasool 4/ 389-90 checked by Al-Arna'ut.

items.ar: وَقَالَ صلى الله عليه وسلم: أَقْرَبُ مَا يَكُونُ الرَّبُّ مِنَ الْعَبْدِ فِي جَوْفِ اللَّيْلِ الآخِرِ فَإِنِ اسْتَطَعْتَ أَنْ تَكُونَ مِمَّنْ يَذْكُرُ اللَّهَ فِي تِلْكَ السَّاعَةِ فَكُنْ
items.en: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: "The closest that the Lord comes to the slave is in the last portion of the night. So, if you are able to be among those who remember Allah in this hour, then be among them."
items.ref: At-Tirmidhi, An-Nasa'i 1/279 and Al-Hakim. See also Al-Albani, Sahih At-Tirmidhi 3/183, and Jdmi'ul-'Usool with Al-Arna'ut's checking 4/144.

items.ar: .وَقَالَ صلى الله عليه وسلم: أَقْرَبُ مَا يَكُونُ الْعَبْدُ مِنْ رَبِّهِ وَهُوَ سَاجِدٌ فَأَكثِرُوا الدُّعَاءَ.
items.en: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: "The closest that the slave comes to his Lord is when he is prostrating, so invoke Allah much (in prostration)."
items.ref: Muslim 1/350.

items.ar: .وَقَالَ صلى الله عليه وسلم: إِنَّهُ لَيُغَانُ عَلَى قَلْبِي وَإِنِّي لأَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ فِي الْيَوْمِ مِائَةَ مَرَّةٍ.
items.en: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: "It is a heavy thing for my heart if I do not seek Allah's forgiveness a hundred times a day."
items.ref: Muslim 4/2075. Ibn 'Athir explains that the Prophet (ﷺ) was always vigilant in his remembrance and drawing near to Allah, and if he forgot to do any of what he normally did from time to time, or it slipped his mind, he felt as if he had wronged himself and so he would begin to seek the forgiveness of Allah. See Jami'ul-'Usool 4/386.

cats.en: The excellence of remembering Allah
cats.ar: فضل التسبيح و التحميد، و التهليل، و التكبير

items.ar: قَالَ صلى الله عليه وسلم: مَنْ قَالَ (سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ) فِي يَوْمٍ مِائَةَ مَرَّةٍ حُطَّتْ خَطَايَاهُ وَلَوْ كَانَتْ مِثْلَ زَبَدِ الْبَحْر.
items.en:
Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: Whoever says:

Glorified is Allah and praised is He.

one hundred times a day, will have his sins forgiven even if they are like the foam of the sea.
items.tr:
Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: Whoever says:
Subḥānallāhi wa biḥamdihi.
one hundred times a day, will have his sins forgiven even if they are like the foam of the sea.
items.ref: Al-Bukhari 7/168, Muslim 4/2071, see also invocation no. 91 of this book.

items.ar: وَقَالَ صلى الله عليه وسلم: كَلِمَتَانِ خَفِيفَتَانِ عَلَى اللِّسَانِ، ثَقِيلَتَانِ فِي الْمِيزَانِ، حَبِيبَتَانِ إِلَى الرَّحْمَنِ: (سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ)، (سُبْحانَ اللَّهِ الْعَظِيمِ)
items.en:
Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: Two words are light on the tongue, weigh heavily in the balance, and are loved by the Most Merciful One:

Glorified is Allah and praised is He, Glorified is Allah the Most Great.
items.tr:
Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: Two words are light on the tongue, weigh heavily in the balance, and are loved by the Most Merciful One:
Subḥānallāhi wa biḥamdih, 
Subḥānallāhi ‘l-`Aẓīm.
items.ref: Al-Bukhari 7/168, Muslim 4/2072.

items.ar: وَقَالَ صلى الله عليه وسلم: لَأَنْ أَقُولَ (سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، وَلاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ، وَاللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ)، أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ مِمَّا طَلَعَتْ عَلَيْهِ الشَّمسُ.
items.en:
Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: For me to say:

Glory is to Allah, 
and praise is to Allah, 
and there is none worthy of worship but Allah,
and Allah is the Most Great.

is dearer to me than all that the sun rises upon (i.e. the whole world).
items.tr:
Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: For me to say:
Subḥānallāh, 
walḥamdu lillāh, 
wa lā ilāha illallāh, 
wallāhu 'Akbar 
is dearer to me than all that the sun rises upon (i.e. the whole world).
items.ref: Muslim 4/2072.
ti: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: For me to …

items.ar: وَقَالَ صلى الله عليه وسلم: أَيَعْجِزُ أَحَدُكُم أَنْ يَكْسِبَ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ أَلْفَ حَسَنَةٍ؟ فَسَأَلَهُ سَائِلٌ مِنْ جُلَسَائِهِ كَيْفَ يَكْسِبُ أَحَدُنَا أَلْفَ حَسَنَةٍ؟ قَالَ: يُسَبِّحُ مِائَةَ تَسْبِيحَةٍ، فَيُكتَبُ لَهُ أَلْفُ حَسَنَةٍ أَوْ يُحَطُّ عَنْهُ أَلْفُ خَطِيئَةٍ.
items.en:
Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: "Is anyone of you incapable of earning one thousand Hasanah (rewards) in a day?" 
Someone from his gathering asked, "How can anyone of us earn a thousand Hasanah?" 
He said, "Glorify Allah a hundred times and a thousand Hasanah will be written for you, or a thousand sins will be wiped away."
items.ref: Muslim 4/2073.

items.ar: مَنْ قَالَ (سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ الْعَظِيمِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ) غُرِسَتْ لَهُ نَخْلَةٌ فِي الْجَنَّةِ
items.en:
Whoever says:

Glorified is Allah the Most Great and praised is He.

will have a date palm planted for him in Paradise.
items.tr:
Whoever says: Subḥānallāhi ‘l-'Aẓīmi wa biḥamdih
will have a date palm planted for him in Paradise.
items.ref: At-Tirmidhi 5/511, and Al-Hakim who graded it authentic and Ath-Thahabi agreed 1/501. See also Al-Albani, Sahihul-Jami' As-Saghir 5/531 and Sahih At-Tirmidhi3/160.

items.ar: وَقَالَ صلى الله عليه وسلم: يَا عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ قَيْسٍ أَلاَ أَدُلُّكَ عَلَى كَنْزٍ مِنْ كُنُوزِ الْجَنَّةِ؟ فَقُلْتُ: بَلَى يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، قَالَ: قُلْ (لاَ حَوْلَ وَلاَ قُوَّةَ إِلاَّ بِاللَّهِ).
items.en:
Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: "O Abdullah bin Qais, should I not point you to one of the treasures of Paradise?" 
I said, "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." 
So he told me to say:
There is no power and no might except by Allah.
items.tr:
Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: "O Abdullah bin Qais, should I not point you to one of the treasures of Paradise?" 
I said, "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." 
So he told me to say:
Lā ḥawla wa lā quwwata 'illā billāh.
items.ref: Al-Bukhari, cf. Al-Asqalani, Fathul-Bari 11/213, Muslim 4/2076.

items.ar: وَقَالَ صلى الله عليه وسلم: أَحَبُّ الْكَلاَمِ إِلَى اللَّهِ أَرْبَعٌ: (سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ)، وَ(الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ)، وَ(لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ)، وَ(اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ)، لاَ يَضُرُّكَ بِأَيِّهِنَّ بَدَأتَ
items.en:
Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: The most beloved words to Allah are four:

Glorified is Allah, 
and
The praise is for Allah, 
and
There is none worthy of worship but Allah, 
and
Allah is the Most Great.
items.tr:
Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: The most beloved words to Allah are four:
Subḥānallāh
Walḥamdu lillāh.
Wa lā ilāha illallāh
Wallāhu Akbar.
items.ref: Muslim 3/1685.
ti: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: The most beloved …

items.ar: جَاءَ أَعْرَابِيٌّ إِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ: عَلِّمْنِي كَلاماً أَقُولُهُ: قَالَ: قُلْ (لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لاَ شَرِيكَ لَهُ، اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ كَبِيراً، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ كَثِيراً، سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ رَبِّ العَالَمِينَ، لاَ حَوْلَ وَلاَ قُوَّةَ إِلاَّ بِاللَّهِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَكِيمِ). قَالَ: فَهَؤُلاَءِ لِرَبِّي، فَمَا لِي؟ قَالَ: قُلْ (اللَّهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لِي، وَارْحَمْنِي، وَاهْدِنِي، وَارْزُقْنِي).
items.en:
A desert Arab came to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) and said, "Teach me a word that I can say. " The Prophet told him to say:

There is none worthy of worship but Allah, Who has no partner, 
Allah is the Great, the Most Great, 
and praise is to Allah in abundance, 
glory is to Allah, Lord of the worlds. 
There is no power and no might but by Allah the Mighty, the Wise.

He said, "That is for my Lord, but what about me?" The Prophet (ﷺ) told him to say:

O Allah forgive me, and have mercy on me and guide me, and provide for me.
items.tr:
A desert Arab came to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) and said, "Teach me a word 
that I can say. " The Prophet told him to say: Lā ilāha illallāh
waḥdahu lā sharīka lah, 
Allāhu Akbaru kabīra, 
walḥamdu lillāhi kathīra, 
Subḥānallāhi Rabbil-`ālamīn, 
Lā ḥawla wa lā quwwata illā billāhi ‘l-`Azīzil-Hakīm.

He said, "That is for my Lord, but what about me?" The Prophet (ﷺ) told 
him to say:
Allāhummaghfir lī, warḥamnī, waḥdinī warzuqnī.
items.ref: Muslim 4/2072, Abu Dawud reports the same Hadith with the addition: and when the Arab left, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "He has filled his hands with goodness." 1/220.

items.ar: كَانَ الرَّجُلُ إِذَا أَسْلَمَ عَلَّمَهُ النَّبيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم الصَّلاَةَ ثُمَّ أَمَرَهُ أَنْ يَدْعُوَ بِهَؤُلاَءِ الْكَلِمَاتِ: (اللَّهُمَّ اغْفِرِ لِي، وَارْحَمْنِي، وَاهْدِنِي، وَعَافِنِي وَارْزُقْنِي)
items.en:
Whenever anyone accepted Islam, the Prophet (ﷺ) used to teach him how to pray then he would instruct him to invoke Allah with the following words:

O Allah forgive me, and have mercy on me and guide me and give me good health and provide for me.
items.tr:
Whenever anyone accepted Islam, the Prophet (ﷺ) used to teach him how to 
pray then he would instruct him to invoke Allah with the following words: Allāhummaghfir lī, warḥamnī, waḥdinī, wa `āfinī warzuqnī.
items.ref: Muslim 4/2073, and in one of Muslim's reports there is the addition: 'For these words combine [the goodness of] this world and the next.'

items.ar: إِنَّ أَفْضَلَ الدُّعَاءِ (الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ)، وَأَفْضَلَ الذِّكْرِ (لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ)
items.en:
The most excellent invocation is:

Praise is for Allah.

and the most excellent words of remembrance are:

There is none worthy of worship but Allah.
items.tr:
The most excellent invocation is: Alḥamdulillāh

and the most excellent words of remembrance are:
Lā ilāha illallāh.
items.ref: At-Tirmidhi 5/462, Ibn Majah 2/1249, and Al-Hakim who graded it authentic and Ath-Tbahabi agreed 1/503. See Al-Albani, Sahihul-Jami' As-Saghir 1/362.

items.ar: الباقيات الصالحات: (سبحان الله) و(الحمد لله )، و(لا إله إلا الله)، و(الله أكبر)،و (لا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله).
items.en:
The good deeds which endure are:

Glorified is Allah, 
and
The praise is for Allah, 
and
There is none worthy of worship but Allah,
and
Allah is the Most Great,
and
There is no power and no might except by Allah.
items.tr:
The good deeds which endure are: Subḥānallāh.
Walḥamdu lillāh.
Wa lā ilāha illallāh
Wallāhu Akbar
Wa lā ḥawla wa lā quwwata illā billāh.
items.ref: Ahmad (no. 513) (Ahmad Shakir, ed.) and its chain of narration is authentic. See Majma'uz-Zawa'id 1/297. Ibn Hajar mentions it in Bulughul-Maram saying that Ibn Hibban and Al-Hakim considered it authentic.

items.ar: عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَمْرٍو رضي الله عنهما قَالَ: رَأَيْتُ النَّبيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَعْقِدُ التَّسْبِيحَ بِيَمِينِهِ.
items.en:
Abdullah bin 'Amr (RA) said: "I saw the Prophet (ﷺ) counting the 
glorification of his Lord on his right hand."
items.ref: Abu Dawud with a different wording 2/81, and At-Tirmidhi 5/521. See also Al-Albani, Sahihul-Jami'As-Saghir 4/271 (no. 4865).

items.ar: إِذَا كَانَ جُنْحُ اللَّيْلِ – أَوْ أَمْسَيْتُم – فَكُفُّوا صِبْيانَكُم، فَإِنَّ الشَّيَاطِينَ تَنْتَشِرُ حِينَئِذٍ، فَإِذَا ذَهَبَ سَاعَةٌ مِنَ اللَّيلِ فَخَلُّوهُمْ، وَأَغْلِقُوا الأَبْوَابَ وَاذْكُرُوا اسْمَ اللَّهِ؛ فَإِنَّ الشَّيطَانَ لاَ يَفْتَحُ بَاباً مُغلَقاً، وَأَوْكُوا قِرَبَكُمْ، وَاذْكُرُوا اسْمَ اللَّهِ، وَخَمِّرُوا آنِيَتَكُم، وَاذْكُرُوا اسْمَ اللَّهِ، وَلَوْ أَنْ تَعْرُضُوا عَلَيْهَا شَيْئاً، وَأَطْفِئُوا مَصَابِيحَكُمْ.
items.en: When night falls, restrain your children (from going out) because at such time the devils spread about. After a period of time has passed, let them be. Shut your doors and mention Allah’s name, for verily the devil does not open a shut door, tie up your water-skins and mention Allah’s name, cover your vessels with anything and mention Allah’s name and put out your lamps.
items.ref: Al-Bukhari with Al-Fath 10/88 and Muslim 3/1595.
